editorials.head: WE HAVE THE DRINK. WE LACK THE WALK.
editorials.body: Once again a dwarf has been found dead of thirst in a fort with barrels stacked to the ceiling. This is not a supply problem. It is a distance problem, and a priorities problem, and possibly a legs problem. We call on the Overseer to place one barrel, any barrel, within reach of anyone who mines. We are not asking for a tavern. We are asking for a barrel.

editorials.head: 1,981 ARMOR STANDS AND NOT ONE SOLDIER
editorials.body: Quakefocus produced 1,981 armor stands. It had, at peak, a militia of zero. That is a ratio of infinity stands per soldier, which the Business Desk has been told is 'not a ratio'. We disagree. It is the purest ratio ever achieved. We only ask that next time someone checks the order before the second thousand.

editorials.head: WE STILL REMEMBER {record}
editorials.body: {record_fort} will be remembered for many things, but mostly for {record}. The stockrooms are still full of the evidence. We propose that every future fort be issued a sensible limit on everything, and that anything past ten require a signed note from {monarch}. No reply yet. We assume a long letter is being written.

editorials.head: PLEASE RENAME THE 'SAFETY' BURROW
editorials.body: Dwarves were sent to the Safety burrow thirty levels down, and a forgotten beast came up the stairs to meet them. The word 'Safety' is doing a great deal of work in that sentence. We propose a more honest sign: 'Burrow (Downstairs)'. It will save no lives, but it will save the word Safety from further embarrassment.

editorials.head: THE GARBAGE PIT IS A ONE-WAY STREET
editorials.body: Dwarves have died hauling refuse back out of the garbage pit while more was being thrown in. We understand both jobs were on the list. We ask only that they not be on the list at the same time, in the same hole. A pit is for putting things in. Taking them out is called a quarry, and it has a different sign.

editorials.head: A TREE IS NOT A PLACE OF WORK
editorials.body: A miner has died of thirst on a tree branch. We repeat: a miner, a profession famous for being underneath things, died on top of one. How he got there is between him and the gods. How he stayed there is between him and the Overseer. We call for a simple rule: if your job title contains the word 'mine', stay off trees.

editorials.head: OUR ARMY IS ONE DWARF, AND HE IS OFF DUTY
editorials.body: The militia of {fort} has ten places, one captain and nine empty spaces where soldiers should be. The captain is listed as 'Off duty'. We do not blame him. We blame the nine spaces, who have never once turned up. We are at war with {enemy}. Someone should tell the roster.

editorials.head: WHO WILL BE MAYOR? NOBODY, APPARENTLY
editorials.body: The offices of mayor, sheriff, hammerer, dungeon master, champion and chief medical dwarf all stand empty. The chairs are lovely. The nameplates are blank. We would run for office ourselves, but the Herald has been advised that journalists are 'too opinionated for government', which we are choosing to take as a compliment.

editorials.head: THE PRODUCTION ORDER VIOLATION ECONOMY
editorials.body: The mayor's office files a production order violation every week. The fort then fails to produce the ordered item. Another violation is filed. This is, by our count, the only industry in the fort with a perfect output record. We suggest the mayor be awarded a medal, if anyone can be found to make one without violating something.

editorials.head: STOP CUTTING EVERY GEM
editorials.body: Strange moods keep demanding rough gems, and every rough gem has already been cut into something shiny and useless. A fisherdwarf, a butcher and a weaver have all asked. The jeweler says she was 'only following orders'. We say: leave one rough gem in a drawer somewhere. Label it 'for emergencies'. Then lock the drawer.

editorials.head: CHILDREN SHOULD NOT HAVE MOODS
editorials.body: A dwarven child was taken by a strange mood and demanded plant cloth. We have no plant cloth. We have a child in a workshop staring at a loom. We do not know who let the child near a workshop, or why the gods considered a child qualified, but we suggest a minimum age for divine inspiration. Twelve seems fair.

editorials.head: REMEMBERING FAMINE, DAY 32
editorials.body: Some forts are founded with no drink, no meals and a handful of plants for ten dwarves. The Food Desk still has its notes from one 'famine, day 32'. The menu that day was 'one plant, shared'. Reviews were mixed. We raise this only so that the next fort's founders pack a lunch. A large lunch. Several barrels of lunch.

editorials.head: THE MEAT WATCH: NEVER AGAIN
editorials.body: A fort once went so long without meat or fish that its paper kept a daily column called the Meat Watch. It ran for longer than some nobles. Thirteen dogs lived in that fort. The Food Desk has never asked what happened to the dogs, and we would ask readers to extend us the same courtesy.

editorials.head: FOUR HOSPITALS, TWO DOCTORS
editorials.body: The Overseer once built four hospitals. Two had no doctor. The other two had a doctor each, who spent the season walking between all four looking for patients who were looking for them. We propose fewer hospitals and more doctors, or at minimum one sign per hospital reading 'nobody is coming, sorry'.

editorials.head: THE CHIEF MEDICAL DWARF CHAIR IS COLD
editorials.body: {fort} has no chief medical dwarf. The office is furnished, the traction bench is polished and the soap is unopened. Patients are treated by whoever walks past, which is usually a hauler holding a stone. We ask anyone with a steady hand and a weak sense of self-preservation to apply. The pay is a chair.

editorials.head: SIXTEEN THOUSAND SMOOTHING JOBS IS TOO MANY
editorials.body: The Overseer once queued 16,000 smoothing jobs for three smoothers. At a generous rate, that is several lifetimes of polishing, which is roughly the point at which a wall stops being a wall and starts being a mirror. We like smooth walls. We like eating more. We ask the Overseer to consider which comes first.

editorials.head: ON GATHERING PLANTS ACROSS THE WHOLE MAP IN THE RAIN
editorials.body: Once again the Overseer has sent every free dwarf to the far edge of the map to pick a berry in a downpour. We admire the ambition. We question the berry. A dwarf soaked to the beard for one sprig of something purple is not a harvest. It is a cry for help, written in mud.

editorials.head: {past_fort} {past_fort_fate}. WE REMEMBER
editorials.body: We do not like to dwell on {past_fort}, which lasted {past_fort_years} and then {past_fort_fate}. But somebody has to. Somewhere in those halls are our beds, our loose stones and at least one mug with a name scratched on it. We would like them back. We would also like whoever has them to wipe their feet.

editorials.head: BRING BACK THE NUANCED HAMLET
editorials.body: Our artifact The Nuanced Hamlet is still in Searabbeys, presumably now admired by goblins who do not understand it. A goblin cannot appreciate nuance. A goblin can barely appreciate a hamlet. We call for a recovery expedition, staffed by volunteers, led by the militia, which is to say by one dwarf, who is off duty.

editorials.head: WE LEFT AN ARTIFACT IN {past_fort}
editorials.body: Somewhere in {past_fort} sits an artifact we made with our own hands and our own strange moods, now dusted by whoever moved in. We find this a tragedy of furniture. We call for a recovery expedition, staffed by volunteers and led by the militia, which is to say by one dwarf, who is off duty.

editorials.head: WHAT 'TOTAL WAR' MEANS, FOR READERS WHO ASKED
editorials.body: {civ} are at war with {enemy}. Readers ask what war means. It means all of it. All of the war. Readers then ask what we are doing about it. We are writing this editorial. The militia is doing nothing, but in a very organized way, from a bench, with excellent posture.

editorials.head: SKIRMISHING IS NOT A HOBBY
editorials.body: We are told we are merely 'skirmishing' with the {enemy_race} bands of {enemy}, a word that makes war sound like a lawn game. It is not a lawn game. Skirmishes involve spears and the general lack of a lawn. We ask the diplomats to clarify whether we are winning, losing, or simply doing it as exercise.

editorials.head: WE ARE AT PEACE WITH A DOZEN GROUPS. NAME ONE
editorials.body: The civilization reports peace with a dozen or more groups. The Herald asked twenty dwarves to name one. Answers included 'the elves?', 'the caravan', 'my cousin' and 'the cat'. The cat is not a group. Still, peace is peace. We ask the diplomat to send us the list so we can be grateful in the right direction.

editorials.head: THERE IS MUCH TO SHARE, AND WE HAVE HEARD IT
editorials.body: The outpost liaison {liaison} arrives each year and opens with 'There is much to share'. He then recommends an import agreement. We have heard the speech so often that the tavern now mouths it along with him. We admire his consistency. We would also admire a second sentence.

editorials.head: RINGS AT 210 PERCENT IS NOT A TRADE DEAL
editorials.body: The liaison has asked for rings at 210% of their value. The Business Desk has studied this figure and concluded that it is a number, and that it is too large. We would pay 210% for a doctor. We would pay 210% for a mayor. We will not pay it for a ring. Rings do not die of thirst. Mostly.

editorials.head: ANOTHER FORT, SAME WORLD, SAME MISTAKES?
editorials.body: {past_fort} lasted {past_fort_years} and then {past_fort_fate}. Now there is {fort}. Every fort starts with hope and ends in the history books. We are not saying the Overseer has a pattern. We are saying the pattern has an Overseer. Let this be the fort where we learn. Let this be the fort with a barrel next to the miners.

editorials.head: ON THE GREAT REWINDS
editorials.body: Several times now the world has stopped, gone dark, and started again from a moment ago. The priests call these the Great Rewinds. Dwarves who lived through one report having the same breakfast twice. We do not understand the gods. We only ask that, next time, they rewind to before the garbage pit.

editorials.head: WHEN THE GODS BLINK, KEEP WORKING
editorials.body: Last week the gods blinked again, and the whole fort froze mid-step for an unknown length of time. Some dwarves used the pause to reflect. Most simply resumed hauling the same stone. The Religion Desk considers this the correct response. If the heavens hiccup, the stone still needs moving.

editorials.head: THE MIST RING: SCIENCE OR SPA?
editorials.body: The pumps of the mist ring spray water into the air so dwarves can walk through it and feel happy. Our Science Desk confirms it works. Dwarves report feeling refreshed, damp and slightly confused about why they cannot drink it. We suggest a sign: 'Do not open mouth'. They will open their mouths anyway.

editorials.head: THE WINDMILLS ARE NOT GIANTS
editorials.body: Readers have written in alarmed about the tall spinning shapes on the surface. Those are windmills. They power the pumps. They are not giants, they do not want your beard, and they will not stop spinning if you shout at them. We have checked. Several times. Loudly.

editorials.head: ABOUT THE EXECUTION TOWER
editorials.body: The fort has built an execution tower. Nobody has been sentenced, because the hammerer's office is empty. So we have a tower and no hammerer, which is a building waiting for a job description. We suggest it be used as a lookout until somebody volunteers for the less pleasant use. Please nobody volunteer.

editorials.head: THE CATACOMBS ARE FILLING UP. THAT IS THE POINT
editorials.body: Visitors to the catacombs have complained that they are 'getting crowded'. That is what catacombs are for. A quiet catacomb is a sign of a healthy fort. A busy one is a sign of a fort that has met a tree, a garbage pit and a forgotten beast in the same year. We ask mourners to bring a lamp and lower expectations.

editorials.head: THE CISTERN IS FULL. THE MINERS ARE THIRSTY. EXPLAIN
editorials.body: The cistern holds more water than some lakes. A miner two corridors away is listed as 'Thirsty'. Our Science Desk has measured the distance and found it to be 'walkable'. Our Labor Desk has measured the miner and found him to be 'busy'. Somewhere between the two, the thirst paradox lives on.

editorials.head: WHY ARE THE STAIRS SO EASY TO CLIMB?
editorials.body: The forgotten beast that visited the Safety burrow came up the stairs. We designed those stairs. We made them lovely and even and easy to climb. The beast appreciated this. We propose that the stairs to the deep be made deliberately awkward, with uneven steps and a strongly worded door.

editorials.head: 150 GEMS AND NOT A SIP
editorials.body: A fey carpenter once died of thirst beside 150 rough gems. The gems were all needed elsewhere. So, it turned out, was water. We say this to every Overseer: a dwarf can be paid in gems, praised in gems, buried with gems. He cannot drink them. We checked. He checked.

editorials.head: SEVEN SCRAPS OF SILK ARE NOT A STOCKPILE
editorials.body: Seven silk scraps once sat in the stockpile and the ledger declared the fort well supplied with cloth. A fey miner then died waiting for cloth that the ledger said existed. Seven scraps is not a stock. It is a handkerchief, cut up. We ask the bookkeeper to count cloth by the sock, not by the hope.

editorials.head: A WEAVER SHOULD NOT DIE WAITING FOR A ROOM
editorials.body: A possessed weaver once died waiting for the loom room to be built. It was on the list. It was a long list, and a thousand-odd armor stands were ahead of it. We say a weaver possessed by the gods outranks an armor stand. We would have thought this went without saying. It clearly needed saying.

editorials.head: THE REFUGEES DESERVE BEDS
editorials.body: Goblin armies keep emptying towns across {world}, and refugee bands now wander looking for a roof. We have roofs. We have, somewhere, a room full of spare thrones. Nobody sleeps well on a throne, but it is better than a field, and nobody here will ask who sat on it first. Bring a blanket. Bring a drink, just in case.

editorials.head: THE CRAZED HEX IS NOT GOING AWAY
editorials.body: The goblin army called The Crazed Hex emptied Padtufted, Pulledrained and Ironcrowds. Its leaders, Ngumrash Ensebrab and Laba Cócefevu Iwe, are said to be 'efficient'. We are not efficient. We have one soldier. We ask the Overseer to consider building a wall before building a 1,982nd armor stand.

editorials.head: WHO NAMES AN ARMY 'THE VICE OF FINS'?
editorials.body: The Vice of Fins, led by Uslôx Ulutodan, attacked Padtufted. The Military Desk has been unable to learn what the fins are or why they are a vice. We suspect carp. We have always suspected carp. Until proven otherwise, militia members should treat any fish with suspicion and any finned goblin with more.

editorials.head: 48 CLAIMANTS AND ONE PAIR OF GREAVES
editorials.body: The steel greaves called The Amusing Duties were lost at Roughnessslaps in year 68 and have since been claimed by about 48 different figures. They sit at Fieryaged, belonging to everyone and worn by nobody. The Herald would like to be the 49th claimant. Our legs are cold and our case is as good as anyone's.

editorials.head: TRAVEL ADVISORY: CROOKED HORRORS
editorials.body: The crooked horror Omo Fewethauyira is reported near Shadyghosts, and Thone Nìnoana lurks at The Sable Nights. Our Weather Desk does not cover horrors, but it does cover 'conditions', and the conditions near those places are 'large, crooked and hungry'. Travelers are advised to pack an umbrella and a will.

editorials.head: THE ELVES ARE BEING ABDUCTED. WE HAVE FEELINGS
editorials.body: Word comes that elves have been abducted from their forest retreats again. The Herald condemns abduction in all its forms. We would also like to state, for balance, that the elves have never once bought our wooden bins. These two facts are unrelated, and we print them side by side purely for reasons of layout.

editorials.head: EVERYONE ELSE CHANGED LEADERS. WE CANNOT FIND ONE
editorials.body: Four groups across {world} have changed leaders this year. We have not managed to fill a single office. Other groups have too many leaders and we have too few. We propose a trade. The liaison will want 210% for it, plus an import agreement.

editorials.head: THE REFUSE STOCKPILE IS NOT A MYSTERY
editorials.body: Every fort the Overseer builds eventually develops a refuse problem, and every time it is solved by a new refuse problem somewhere else. One fort had loose stones. One had armor stands. One had the garbage pit. We propose a fourth approach: putting things in one place and leaving them there.

editorials.head: {drinks} DRINKS. COUNT THEM. THEN DRINK ONE
editorials.body: The fort currently holds {drinks} drinks. Forts have lost miners to thirst with more than that on hand. A number in a ledger has never quenched anyone. We urge every reader, today, to walk to a barrel and take one sip on behalf of the fort's statistics. Do it for the miners. Do it for the ledger.

editorials.head: THE DRINK IS RUNNING LOW, AND THE OVERSEER IS SMOOTHING
editorials.body: Drink stocks have fallen to {drinks}. In response the Overseer has queued several hundred smoothing jobs, as if a polished wall might be licked for moisture. It cannot. We have asked. We call for brewing first, smoothing second and a written apology to the still, which has been idle for days.

editorials.head: {pop} DWARVES AND NOBODY WANTS TO BE SHERIFF
editorials.body: {fort} is home to {pop} dwarves, and not one of them will be sheriff. We have asked politely. We have asked at the tavern. We have asked a dwarf who was asleep, who did not say no, and who was briefly appointed until he woke up. The search continues. The badge is very shiny.

editorials.head: {stone} STONES AND RISING: HAVE WE LEARNED NOTHING?
editorials.body: A fort before us was buried under loose stones. We now hold {stone}. The Business Desk is not saying history repeats, but history has picked up a stone and is looking at us meaningfully. We call for stockpiles, quarries, a mason with ambition, or at least a very long wall.

editorials.head: WE HAVE {gems} GEMS. PLEASE DO NOT CUT THEM ALL
editorials.body: The fort currently holds {gems} gems. Experience says that within a week the jeweler will have cut every single one, and within a fortnight a mood will demand a rough one. We propose a reserve: a small locked box, a guard (the captain, perhaps, since he is off duty) and a sign saying 'mood use only'.

editorials.head: SEARABBEYS HAD THIRTEEN DOGS. WE HAVE {dogs}
editorials.body: Searabbeys had thirteen dogs and no meat for months, and the Herald never asked any follow-up questions. We now have {dogs} dogs and, we are told, meat. Let us keep it that way. Every dog in {fort} deserves to live in a fort with a butcher who has something else to do.

editorials.head: TWENTY FARM PLOTS DID NOT SAVE US BEFORE
editorials.body: A fort once had twenty farm plots and still ran the Meat Watch for a season. Farms are not dinner. Farms are the rumor of dinner. With {farms} plots in {fort}, we ask the farmers to keep an eye on the cooks, and the cooks to keep an eye on the barrels, and everyone to keep an eye on the Overseer.

editorials.head: {deadname} DESERVED A BARREL NEARBY
editorials.body: We mourn {deadname} this week. Whatever the final cause, the Herald notes that this fort has a long tradition of dwarves dying within sight of everything they needed. We ask the Overseer, again, to look at the map and count the steps between the dwarves and the drink. Then halve them.

editorials.head: {moodname} IS IN A MOOD. WHAT HAVE WE RUN OUT OF?
editorials.body: {moodname} has been seized by a strange mood. History teaches that the item demanded will be the one thing the fort has just used up. Rough gems, plant cloth, a specific bone. We urge every hauler to check every corner, every drawer and every goblin pocket. A dwarf's life may depend on lint.

editorials.head: AN OFFICE IS FILLED. MIRACLES DO HAPPEN
editorials.body: {promoted} has become a {post}, filling one of this fort's famous empty chairs. The Herald congratulates them and would like to warn them that the chair was empty for a reason. That reason was mainly paperwork. The mayor's office has already filed a welcome violation.

editorials.head: PROTECT {artifact} FROM THE NEXT GOBLIN OCCUPATION
editorials.body: {artifact} is the pride of {fort}. So were the treasures we left behind in {past_fort}, which {past_fort_fate}. They now sit in a fort we no longer run. We propose that every artifact be fitted with a small handle, so that when the time comes, someone can carry it out.

editorials.head: TO OUR NEW ARRIVALS: A BRIEF HISTORY
editorials.body: Welcome, migrants. You have joined a fort in a long line. {record_fort} gave the world {record}. Dwarves here have died on trees, in garbage pits and in a burrow called Safety. The beds are good, though. The mist ring is nice. Find the nearest barrel before you unpack.

editorials.head: WHEN THE LIAISON COMES, LET HIM FINISH
editorials.body: Each time {liaison} arrives, someone interrupts him before he can finish recommending the import agreement. Then he starts again. This doubles the meeting. We propose that the fort simply let him finish, nod, and offer him a drink. He has come a long way to say the same thing.

editorials.head: NO, WE WILL NOT GATHER PLANTS IN THE SNOW
editorials.body: The Overseer has again ordered plant gathering on the far side of the map, in the snow. The Weather Desk would like it on record that very little grows in snow except frostbite. Dwarves returning from the expedition carried two berries and a strong grudge. The grudge will keep longer.

editorials.head: SUMMER ON THE SURFACE: A WARNING FROM HISTORY
editorials.body: It is summer, and the surface is bright and full of trees. Please remember that a miner once died on a tree branch. Please remember that the sun is not a lamp you can turn off. Please remember that the Overseer will send you outside to pick something. Bring a waterskin. Bring two.

editorials.head: IN DEFENSE OF THE OVERSEER (SOMEONE HAS TO)
editorials.body: Everyone mocks the Overseer. But consider: fort after fort, one world, never once bored. The Overseer built the mist ring. The Overseer dug the cistern. The Overseer, at great expense, ensured that no dwarf will ever lack an armor stand. Is that so terrible? Yes. But it is also very thorough.

editorials.head: THE OVERSEER SHOULD WALK A DAY IN OUR BOOTS
editorials.body: We invite the Overseer to spend one day as a miner: dig a tunnel, get thirsty, walk forty tiles past a stack of thrones to find a barrel, and discover it was claimed for a work order. We suspect that after one day the orders would change. We suspect it would also be the Overseer's last day.

editorials.head: WHO READS THE WORK ORDERS? A SIMPLE QUESTION
editorials.body: Somewhere there is a list of work orders. On it, in one fort, was a line that said 'armor stand' and a number that kept going. The Business Desk would like to know whether anyone reads this list. If the answer is the Overseer, we ask that the Overseer read it twice, slowly, with a finger.

editorials.head: LETTER TO THE GOBLINS IN OUR OLD FORT
editorials.body: To The Torments of Hating, current residents of Searabbeys: the well sticks in the winter. The third bedroom floods. Please do not throw away the loose stones, they are load-bearing in a spiritual sense. And please return The Nuanced Hamlet, as it was never yours, and you are not nuanced.

editorials.head: SPARE A THOUGHT FOR THE DISTANT LETTER
editorials.body: The Distant Letter were evicted from Searabbeys by goblins, then changed leaders, all within the same history. That is a rough decade. We hope their new leader is calm, well rested and owns a door that locks. If they need a new home, we know a fort with 148 empty thrones.

editorials.head: THE HUMANS AT JACKALDEFENSE SHOULD KNOCK
editorials.body: The humans of The Grooved Council occupied Jackaldefense and evicted The Distinct Dungeon. Everybody in this world, it seems, is moving into somebody else's house. We remind readers to lock their doors, label their mugs and keep a firm hand on their beds. Possession is nine-tenths of the deed.

editorials.head: OTHERS RECLAIM THEIR FORTS. WHY NOT US?
editorials.body: Across {world}, dwarves keep marching back into their lost forts and taking them home. We write editorials. We propose a reclaiming party for {past_fort}, as soon as the militia has more than one dwarf in it and that dwarf is on duty.

editorials.head: GO, OILY BOOTS, GO
editorials.body: The Sport Desk would like to declare its support for The Oily Boots, currently reclaiming Scaldedarch. We do not know their record. We do not know their colors. We know their name is The Oily Boots, and that is enough. Any team called The Oily Boots has our heart, and possibly our socks.

editorials.head: AN OPEN LETTER TO OUR MONARCH
editorials.body: Dear {monarch}: we have lost forts in your name, built you more thrones than you have relatives and kept the war going by not showing up to it. We ask only for a mayor, a doctor and one soldier who is on duty. Also we would like {past_fort} back. Also, respectfully, a raise. Your loyal paper.

editorials.head: THE DIPLOMAT IS WELCOME. THE SPEECH IS LONG
editorials.body: The diplomat is always welcome in {fort}. We would only ask, gently, that the speeches be kept to the length of one meal. Last visit lasted two meals and a nap. The tavern keeper has started serving 'diplomat portions', which are large enough to see a dwarf through a treaty.

editorials.head: SOMEONE IS WATCHING US, AND IT FOLLOWS THE ELVES
editorials.body: Dwarves report the strange feeling of being watched, especially near merchants, diplomats and animal people. The feeling then jumps suddenly to whatever is trying to eat us. The Society Desk cannot explain it but finds it oddly reassuring. At least something notices the beast before it reaches the stairs.

editorials.head: OUR GHOSTS ARE SPREAD ACROSS THREE FORTS
editorials.body: Every fort the Overseer leaves behind keeps its ghosts. {past_fort} surely has a few: a dehydrated miner, perhaps, or a carpenter who died beside a heap of gems. The Religion Desk asks whether ghosts can migrate. If so, we would like them to come home, have a drink, and finally rest.

editorials.head: A MEMORIAL FOR BOMREK ENSHALCATTEN
editorials.body: Bomrek Enshalcatten, miner of Searabbeys, was found dead, dehydrated, in a fort holding 1,994 drinks. The Herald proposes a small memorial: a single barrel, placed beside every mine shaft in {fort}, with a plaque that reads 'For Bomrek. Drink it.' Several readers have already volunteered to test the barrel.

editorials.head: A TRIBUTE TO THE OLD PAPER OF {past_fort}
editorials.body: Before us there was the paper of {past_fort}, a fine sheet that covered every famine with tremendous restraint. We tip our hats to its staff, who reported the last days, as {past_fort} {past_fort_fate}, without once using a rude word. We have not been so disciplined.

editorials.head: DEAR URIST: I INHERITED A THRONE
editorials.body: Dear Urist, my late uncle left me a throne in {past_fort}. That fort {past_fort_fate}. Is it still mine? — Throne Heir. Dear Heir: legally, yes. Practically, it belongs to whoever is sitting on it, and that is probably a goblin. Do not go and ask him to stand up. — Urist

editorials.head: DEAR URIST: WHERE IS SAFE?
editorials.body: Dear Urist, when the alarm rings, where should I go? Not the Safety burrow, I am told. — Nervous. Dear Nervous: correct. Not the trees either, not the garbage pit, and not the stairs. My advice is the tavern. Nobody safe has ever been found there, but nobody sober has either. — Urist

editorials.head: DEAR URIST: SHOULD I JOIN THE MILITIA?
editorials.body: Dear Urist, the militia has nine empty places. Should I join? — Curious Hauler. Dear Curious: if you join, you double the army. That is a 100% increase, the largest in the fort's history. You will also be off duty, so the risk is mostly to your posture. I say go. — Urist

editorials.head: DEAR URIST: WHAT DO I DO WITH AN ARMOR STAND?
editorials.body: Dear Urist, I have been issued an armor stand. I own no armor. — Puzzled. Dear Puzzled: you are part of a great tradition. Forts before us issued them by the thousand to dwarves who also owned no armor. Hang a hat on it. Hang a sock. Tell your friends it is art. It is, at this point. — Urist

editorials.head: WHY DO DWARVES DIE BESIDE BARRELS? A STUDY
editorials.body: Our Science Desk has studied the thirst paradox across fort after fort. Findings: dwarves are not dying for lack of drink, but for lack of time to fetch it. The cure is fewer jobs or closer barrels. The Overseer reviewed our study and responded by queuing another 400 smoothing jobs. Study ongoing.

editorials.head: REFUSE HAULING IS NOT A CONTACT SPORT
editorials.body: Some dwarves have been treating the garbage pit like a sport, hauling refuse in and out against the clock. It is not a sport. Dwarves died the last time two teams played it at once. The Sport Desk has suspended the league indefinitely, and the trophy, a dented bucket, has been retired.

editorials.head: AUTUMN REVIEW: HOW IS THIS FORT DOING?
editorials.body: With autumn here, the Herald grades the fort. Drink: present, if you walk. Offices: empty. Militia: one, off duty. Goblins: at war, at a distance. Artifacts: some, guarded by nobody. Compared with {past_fort} at this stage, we are doing well. That is, admittedly, a low bar.

editorials.head: SPRING: THIS YEAR WILL BE DIFFERENT
editorials.body: Every spring the Herald writes that this year will be different. This spring we mean it. The miners will drink. The orders will stop at a sensible number. The Safety burrow will be safe. Someone will be mayor. We will reprint this editorial next spring, unchanged, as is our tradition.

editorials.head: DID WE ALREADY LIVE THIS WEEK?
editorials.body: Several readers report that, after the last Great Rewind, they dug the same tunnel twice and lost the same argument twice. The Science Desk confirms that time went backwards a little. It cannot confirm whether the argument was lost fairly. We advise all dwarves to write important wins down, in case the gods blink again.

editorials.head: A PORTRAIT OF OUR ARMY, IN FULL
editorials.body: For the first time, the Herald presents the entire militia of {fort} in a single portrait. Here he is: the captain, seated, off duty, holding a mug. The nine empty places are represented by nine empty chairs. {enemy} has been sent a copy. We hope it frightens them. It frightens us.

editorials.head: A CHECKLIST FOR WHOEVER BUILDS THE NEXT FORT
editorials.body: One: barrels before beds. Two: stop at ten armor stands. Three: no burrow called Safety. Four: keep one rough gem. Five: miners stay off trees. Six: never haul from a pit while filling it. Seven: name a mayor. Eight: reread one through seven. We will mail this to every future fort in this world.

letters.body: I have been assigned to make armor stands. I asked how many. I was told 'until further notice'. I have read the history pages. I would like the further notice now, please, before the first thousand.

I am a miner and I would like to propose a barrel at the end of every tunnel. I am not asking for comfort. I am asking not to become a cautionary tale in your pages like the miners in your history pages.
letters.by: A Miner Who Read The History

letters.body: I hereby refuse to enter any burrow named Safety. Rename it 'Danger' and I will go there happily, on the grounds that nothing in this fort has ever been what it says it is.
There is a miner on a tree branch again. I know the history. I am not climbing up there. I am writing to the Herald so it is on record that somebody noticed.
This week I was told to throw refuse in the garbage pit. An hour later I was told to haul it back out. I did neither. I would rather be charged by the mayor than be number nine.
I volunteered for the militia. I was told the squad was 'full'. I looked. There is one captain and nine empty places. I am beginning to think the empty places have a union.
As captain of the militia, I wish to respond to recent jokes. I am not 'always off duty'. I am waiting for orders. The orders say 'Off duty'. I am, therefore, on duty at being off duty.

I received a production order violation for failing to make a crown. I am a fisherdwarf. I do not know how to make a crown. I do not know who ordered a crown. I would like to be charged with something I can at least spell.

Nobody will be sheriff, so I have begun policing the corridors myself. So far I have arrested a cat, a bucket and myself, by accident. Please appoint someone qualified before I arrest the mayor's office.
letters.by: A Concerned Citizen With A Stick

letters.body: I was asked whether I would like to be hammerer. I asked what it involved. They pointed at the execution tower. I said I had a prior engagement. They asked when. I said 'forever'.

Why do we have an office for a dungeon master but no dungeon? Or rather, why do we have a dungeon but no master? Or is the dungeon the empty office? I have been thinking about this all week instead of hauling.
Our champion's office is empty. I am willing to be champion, as long as there is no fighting involved. I am very good at standing heroically. I have been practicing at the mist ring.
I have a feeling a mood is coming. I do not know what I will need. Please, I beg the jeweler, stop cutting the rough gems until I find out. I will repay you in artifacts.
My child has taken over a workshop and is demanding plant cloth. The Overseer has queued 'smoothing'. I would like the record to show that I asked for cloth first and smoothing never.

I am thirsty. There are {drinks} drinks in this fort. I have been assigned to gather plants on the far side of the map. I would like to know which of these facts the Overseer considers the important one.

My grandfather was at {past_fort}, back when the meat ran out. He still flinches when anyone says 'fish'. He wanted me to tell your readers to eat their meat while there is meat. He says it is the only advice he has.
I survived {record_fort}. I helped make {record}, personally. I am not proud. I am not ashamed. I am tired. If anyone in this fort orders more than ten of anything, please wake me so I can leave.

I have read that there is a room full of thrones sitting in {past_fort}. I have never sat on a throne in my life. Could the next caravan bring one back? Just one. I will sit on it carefully and give it back.
We are at war with {enemy}. I have never seen one of them. Is it possible we are winning by being impossible to find? If so, I recommend we keep doing whatever we are doing, which is nothing.
I would like to know why we are at war with {enemy} but have only ONE soldier, and he is sitting down. I am not a general, but I have counted my fingers, and it does not seem enough.
The liaison stopped me in the hall and said 'There is much to share'. I said I did not have anything to share. He recommended an import agreement. I am a child. I have one sock. He wrote it down.
I make rings. I heard the liaison wanted rings at 210 percent. I made some. He has now decided he wants something else at 210 percent. I have 40 rings and a grudge.
I would like to defend {liaison}. He has a hard job, travels in all weather, and says the same sentence every year because nobody has ever let him get to the second one. Let the man speak.

I walked through the mist ring today and felt happy for the first time in a season. Then I remembered I was thirsty and the mist cannot be drunk. Then I felt sad. Then I walked back through it. Net happiness: even.
The windmills creak all night. I have been told this is the sound of happiness being pumped into the mist ring. My happiness would be greater if the windmills stopped creaking.

The execution tower has the best view in {fort}. Nobody goes up there because of the name. I go up every evening. It is lovely. I have started calling it the Observation Tower, and nobody has stopped me.
Could whoever keeps visiting the catacombs at night please stop humming? It is very atmospheric but I sleep two walls away, and frankly the dead were here first.
I fell in the cistern. I was in there for an hour. I came out and was assigned to gather plants. Nobody asked if I was all right. I was, but it would have been nice to be asked.

I am one of the fort's smoothers. My queue currently holds more jobs than I have days left in my life. I have made my peace with it. I would like to be buried in a smooth coffin, smoothed by me, in advance.
I was sent to gather plants across the whole map in the rain. I returned with one strawberry and a cold. The strawberry was eaten by somebody else. The cold, I kept.
Could someone put a door on the stairs to the deep? A strong one. With a lock. I know beasts can break doors, but it would at least make them knock first, which is only polite.

I went to the hospital with a broken arm. Nobody was there. I went to the other hospital. Nobody was there either. I set the arm myself. It is now mostly pointing the right way. Please appoint a doctor.
We have no chief medical dwarf. I have been diagnosing my friends by looking at them and saying 'that looks bad'. I am right every time. I am happy to take the job if it comes with soap.
I hear refugees from the burned towns are wandering the world. Send them here. We have beds, a mist ring and a militia position open for nine of them. Ask them to bring their own drink, just in case.

My cousin lived in Ironcrowds until The Crazed Hex came. She arrived here with nothing but a bucket. She asked where the army was. I pointed at the captain. She asked where the rest was. I pointed at the chairs.

During the last Great Rewind I lost an entire afternoon of work. I had smoothed four tiles. When the world resumed, they were rough again. I do not blame the gods. I blame whoever was keeping the gods awake.
The gods blinked again yesterday. Everyone froze. I suggest that, next time, we all agree to freeze in heroic poses, so if the world ends mid-blink, history remembers us as a very good-looking fort.
I once saw The Nuanced Hamlet up close, back at Searabbeys. I cannot describe it. That is the nuance. Now the goblins have it and I would like to know whether they appreciate it, or just sit on it.

I held Claspedserpent once at Quakefocus, before it was put in a cabinet. It is heavy and silver and very pretty. I did not hit anyone with it. I would like credit for that, as everyone else in the room was asking for it.
I want to thank the Overseer for my bedroom. It is smooth, warm and has a door. I am told the Overseer queued 4,000 other rooms just like it. I am the only one finished. I feel very special.
To the Overseer: please, for one season, order nothing new. Let us finish one thing. Any thing. Let us look upon a completed job and know peace. Then go back to ordering armor stands if you must.
I think the Overseer is doing a fine job and everyone should stop complaining. I would write more, but I have just been assigned to haul 300 stones to a stockpile that has not been built.
I confess I am one of the dwarves who threw refuse in the garbage pit while others were hauling it out. I did not know. Nobody tells the throwers what the haulers are doing. I would like a bell.

I propose banning all trees within a day's walk of the fort. They are unsafe, unhelpful and, according to history, deadly to miners. The elves will object. The elves object to everything we do anyway.

Every time someone dies near a tree, everyone blames the tree. The tree was simply standing there, as trees do. Perhaps we blame the dwarf who climbed it, or the Overseer who sent him. Leave the tree out of it.
Dear captain, I see you sitting alone in the barracks, off duty, every day. If you would like company, I am off duty too, as a matter of temperament. We could be off duty together. Bring a mug.
I was born in {past_fort}, in a room with 22 thrones in it. I thought every room had thrones. Moving here, I asked where the thrones were. Everyone laughed. I am still sitting on the floor.

Drink stocks are down to {drinks}. The still is idle. The brewer is smoothing a wall. The miners are watching the brewer with an expression I do not like. Someone please intervene before history repeats.

My mother was at {past_fort} through its famine. She says the founders brought seventeen plants and a great deal of optimism. She says they ate the optimism first. She still keeps a plant in her pocket.
Does our monarch {monarch} know we exist? I have written to him four times about the empty offices. The only reply was from the liaison, recommending an import agreement.
We are at peace with a dozen groups. I would like to meet one of them. Just one. Ideally the one with the best food. Could the diplomat arrange a small, friendly dinner?
I hereby lay claim to The Amusing Duties, the steel greaves at Fieryaged. I base my claim on the fact that 48 others have done so and nothing happened to them either. I would like them delivered.
I have heard there is a goblin army called The Vice of Fins. I have long suspected that the carp and the goblins were in league. I now have proof, in the form of a name. I rest my case.

Lately I have the feeling something is watching me, especially when merchants are near. Then it stops watching me and goes to look at a goblin instead. I am almost offended. I am more interesting than a goblin.
I tried to drink from the mist ring. It does not work. I tried for an hour. I am now very damp and still thirsty, which I am told is the most traditional way to be thirsty in this world.

I am told this is not the first fort in this world. I would like to know what happens to us when the Overseer starts a fourth. Do we go too? Do we stay? Do the goblins get our rooms? I need to know whether to unpack.
My uncle's ghost still haunts {past_fort}. He died beside 150 gems. I worry about him. Is anyone in that fort making sure he has company? The goblins, perhaps? He always liked an argument.

I am the fort's refuse hauler, and I wish to say that the work is honest, smelly and necessary. Please do not throw anything into the pit while I am in it. That is all I ask. That is all any of us ever asked.
The visiting diplomat complimented my beard. I have written down the date. I intend to celebrate it yearly. I recommend all dwarves try to get a compliment from a diplomat, it lasts for weeks.

I read that another dwarven band marched home and reclaimed its old fort. Why can they reclaim forts and we cannot even reclaim a sock from the laundry? I demand a reclaiming expedition, starting with my sock.

Why was the Safety burrow thirty levels down? Safe from what? The things that live thirty levels down? I have a modest proposal: the next Safety burrow should be in the tavern, where at least you are among friends.

I cleaned the mayor's office this week. Nobody has sat at the desk in years, but the outbox is full of production order violations. I do not know who is writing them. I have started sleeping with a candle.

There is a work order on the board for 'thrones (repeat)'. I have taken it down three times. It is back each morning. I am writing in case I disappear and someone needs to know why there are suddenly a hundred and forty-eight thrones.

{moodname} is in a strange mood and has been staring at the same workshop for days. If anyone has a rough gem, plant cloth or a bone of anything, please bring it at once. Do not cut it first. Do not smooth it.
I knew {deadname}. They were kind, funny, and always knew where the nearest barrel was, which in this fort is a rare gift. Please, everyone, raise a mug, and then go and drink it, in their honour.
To {promoted}, our new {post}: congratulations, and good luck. Advice from a dwarf who has watched these chairs stay empty: do not open the mayor's outbox. Do not read the work orders. Drink often.
To the new migrants: the tavern is that way, the barrels are that way, and the trees are absolutely not that way. If anyone sends you to the Safety burrow, smile, nod, and go to the tavern.
Could the caravan please take some of our extra furniture? We have more armor stands than the merchants have wagons. I asked the merchant to make an offer. He offered to leave quietly.
{masterwright} has made a masterwork {masterwork}. I would like to propose we put it somewhere a goblin occupation cannot reach. History suggests that nowhere qualifies, but let us at least try.

I was sent outside in the snow to gather plants. There are no plants. There is snow. I have brought back some snow. I have been assigned to store it. I would like to file a complaint with an office that has someone in it.
With {pop} of us now, the dining hall is full, the beds are full and the hospital is still empty. I find this pattern instructive. Perhaps we should build fewer thrones and more doctors.
There are only {pop} of us. I miss the bustle of {past_fort}, where you could not walk five steps without tripping over an armor stand. Here you can walk forever and meet nobody. It is unsettling.
I have hidden a rough gem somewhere in the fort. I will not say where. When the next mood comes and demands one, come to me. I will reveal it, for a modest fee and the title of 'Gem Keeper'.
We have no meat again. My grandmother remembers the last meatless winter and has started looking at the dogs in a way the dogs do not appreciate. Please send hunters before she does.
There are {dogs} dogs in the fort. That is more dogs than soldiers by quite a margin. I propose we enlist them. They are loyal, brave and, unlike the captain, they are never off duty.
We are low on wood and the Overseer has ordered beds, barrels, bins and, I fear, thrones. I would like to know which of these the Overseer plans to make out of feelings.
We have {farms} farm plots now. A fort before us had twenty and still had no meat. I do not want to sound gloomy, but I have started growing a small private mushroom behind my bed, just in case.
We have struck {mineral}. Good. Wonderful, even. Please do not let anyone turn it into two thousand of anything. Ten is plenty. Ten is a lovely number.
It is summer, the surface is lovely, and I have been ordered to cut trees all day. I keep looking up at the branches. I know the history. I am cutting from the ground. Please do not ask me to climb.

Autumn is here and someone has queued harvest jobs in every field at once, on every edge of the map. Our farmers will spend all season walking. Please, could we pick the close plants first and the far plants never?
Spring again. Every spring someone writes that this year will be different. I would like to be that someone this year. This year will be different. I will report back in winter.
It is winter and the well has frozen. I have been told the cistern has plenty. I have been told the barrels have plenty. I have been told to gather plants. I have been told a lot this winter.
I wish to report that I am on strike. I would like to explain my demands, but the office I would hand them to is empty. I have left them on the mayor's desk, beside the violations.
I write in reply to the reader who defended the Overseer. Sir, you were assigned to haul 300 stones to a stockpile that does not exist. You are not a defender. You are a hostage with good manners.

In reply to the captain's letter: being on duty at being off duty is the finest piece of military reasoning I have read. I would like to enlist purely to serve under a mind like that. Also I am tired.
To the Refuse Hauler: I am one of the throwers. I did not know you were down there. I will ring a bell from now on. I have no bell. I will shout 'bell'. Please listen for it.
To the elf defending trees: the tree may have been 'simply standing there', but it was simply standing there with a miner in it for an entire season. A good neighbour would have said something.

To the dwarf who inherited a throne in a lost fort: I also inherited one. Perhaps we could go together and ask the new owners to share. They will say no, but at least we will have company being refused.
As bookkeeper I must correct the fort's folklore. The number of armor stands at Quakefocus was not 'about two thousand'. It was 1,981. I counted. It took a season. I would like that season back.
Again, as bookkeeper: Searabbeys held 1,994 drinks when Bomrek died, not 2,000. The six missing drinks have never been accounted for. I have my suspicions. They are all named after the miners.
I believe I saw the ghost of the possessed weaver from {past_fort} last night, standing in front of our loom room. It looked very relieved that ours is built. I left it some thread, as a courtesy.
I have found seven silk scraps in the stockpile and I am frightened. Last time seven silk scraps were all we had, a miner died believing there was cloth. Please, someone weave something real.

I have no opinion on import agreements, but I wish to state that the liaison's hat is magnificent and I would trade a great deal for it. If anyone sees him, please ask whether the hat is part of the agreement.

I have written down everything the liaison said this year and compared it to last year's notes. They are identical, down to the cough. I believe he is reading from a card. I would like to see the card.
If we are at war with {enemy}, why do we have thousands of armor stands in an old fort and no armor in this one? I am not asking for a stand. I am asking for a helmet. I would hang it on myself.
I have looked at the world map. {enemy} are a long way off. Their friends are a long way off. The garbage pit is very close. I know which one I am more afraid of.
Has anyone considered that the goblins may be as disorganised as we are? Perhaps their militia is also one goblin, off duty. Perhaps the war is two benches facing each other across the world.

I used to read the old paper at {record_fort}. It printed the count of {record} every day, like weather. Everyone checked it at breakfast. I miss it. Could the Herald run a daily count of something? Anything?

Your paper prints a great deal about dead forts and very little about my sculpture. I accept that a miner on a tree branch is news. I would argue that my sculpture of a miner on a tree branch is also news.

I would like to thank the Herald for reminding us every issue that we could all die beside a barrel. It has made me drink more water than ever. I have never felt better. I have also never left the tavern.
I have started carrying a mug at all times. If I die of thirst, it will not be because I lacked a mug. It will be because the Overseer gave me a job six levels away from anything to put in it.
If you are fey, take my advice: ask for something common. A rock. A log. Do not ask for rough gems, plant cloth or silk. The fort will not have them. The fort will never have them. Ask for a rock.
I was one floor above the Safety burrow when the forgotten beast went by on the stairs. It looked at me. It kept going down. I do not know why. I have never felt more insulted or more alive.
The Overseer has designated plant gathering on every bush across the entire map. I have started to suspect the Overseer has never seen the map and simply assumes the far side is a short walk.

A dwarf from the lower dormitory attacked one of the windmills yesterday, believing it to be a giant. The windmill won. The dwarf has been taken to the hospital, where, as is tradition, there was nobody.

I would like to run for mayor on a single promise: I will never file a production order violation. Not once. The office will be quiet, the outbox empty and everyone may make what they like. Vote for me.
I oppose the candidate promising no violations. Without them, how will we know that we have failed? A fort needs its paperwork. I am running on a platform of more violations, but nicer ones.

Last week I held a picnic at the top of the execution tower. Several friends attended. The view was lovely, the bread was fresh, and nobody was executed. I recommend it to all, on that last condition.
Before the last Great Rewind, {citizen2} owed me a mug of ale. After it, they say the debt never happened. I believe the gods rewound the world specifically to avoid paying. I would like it noted.

I arrived here with a refugee band after we were driven out of our home. The fort has been kind. I have been given a bed, a job and, unexpectedly, an armor stand. I do not know why. I have hung my coat on it.
Why do we not trade more with the humans of The Fair Cakes at Toeembrace? With a name like that, they must have cakes. We have stone. Stone and cake is the basis of a strong friendship.
I was planning a trip to Shadyghosts. Then I read about Omo Fewethauyira, the crooked horror. I have cancelled my trip. I have also cancelled my plans to say the word 'Shadyghosts' out loud.
Four groups have changed leaders this year. We have no mayor. I suggest we borrow one of their old leaders. Surely someone has a spare, slightly used, with a few good years of paperwork left.

My daughter had a strange mood last month and demanded plant cloth. We found some, just in time. She made a magnificent artifact. She is nine. She now refuses to tidy her room because she is 'legendary'.
After decades of smoothing, I have retired. I leave behind 3,412 smooth tiles and a queue of 12,588 more. I wish my replacement well. I recommend a comfortable stool and a deep acceptance of fate.

letters_abroad.body: I write from {town}, where the humans keep their drink in one place and walk to it when thirsty. It is astonishing. Nobody has died beside a barrel all season. I asked how they manage it. They said 'we just go and get some'. I am taking notes for the Overseer.

The humans of {town} asked me what dwarves are famous for. I said craftsmanship. They said they had heard it was armor stands. Word has spread, apparently. I told them that was a different fort. It was not a different fort.
{town} has a mayor. He sits in an office, talks to people and goes home. I watched him for a week, hoping to bring back the secret. As far as I can tell, the secret is that somebody agreed to do it.

The town guard of {town} has forty members, all on duty, all at once. I could not believe it. I asked where they found so many people willing to stand up. They asked how many we have. I changed the subject to beards.

The humans of {town} let their children climb trees. For fun. I explained what happened to the miner on the branch. They laughed and said miners should not climb trees. I agreed, and then I had to sit down for a while.

I fell ill in {town} and was taken to a hospital that contained a doctor. A real one, standing in it, on purpose. I was so surprised I recovered on the spot. They billed me for the visit. Worth every coin.
The humans of {town} throw their rubbish in a pit and then, and I wish to stress this, leave it there. Nobody goes in after it. I watched for three days. I have never seen anything so restful.

The folk of {town} say the folk of {town2} are lazy. The folk of {town2} say the same of {town}. I have visited both. Neither has made more than ten of any one item, ever. To a dwarf, both towns look lazy and wise.

In {town} they sell gems uncut, rough, as they came out of the ground. I bought six. I am carrying them home in my sock. The next time somebody at {fort} has a strange mood, they are to come to me first.

I met the outpost liaison {liaison} at an inn in {town}. He told the innkeeper there was much to share and recommended an import agreement for the soup. The innkeeper agreed, which I think encourages him.
Everyone in {town} is talking about {enemy}. They asked how our defences are. I said we have one captain and nine chairs. They thought I was joking. I let them think so. It seemed kinder.

{town} is full of refugees from towns the goblins burned. They sleep in the market and ask every dwarf they meet for a fort with beds. I have been telling them about {fort}. I have not mentioned the trees.

A scholar in {town} has written a history of our forts. The chapter on {past_fort} is short. It says it lasted {past_fort_years} and then {past_fort_fate}. The footnotes are longer, and mostly about barrels.
The humans of {town} have heard of {record}. It is taught in their schools as an example of 'not checking the order'. I told them I knew someone from {record_fort}. They asked for an autograph.

The elves of {retreat} were horrified to hear a miner died in a tree. Not for the miner. For the tree. They have held a ceremony to cleanse it, though it is many days away. I asked if they would hold one for the miner. They are thinking it over.

I offered the elves of {retreat} a gift of wooden thrones from our surplus. They wept, held a funeral for the wood and returned the thrones with a note. The note said 'how many of these do you have'. I did not reply.

The elves of {retreat} drink from the stream whenever they are thirsty. No queue, no work order, no forty-tile walk. I mentioned this to an elf and she asked why anyone would do it differently. I had no good answer.

Even the elves of {retreat} do not gather plants across the whole map in the rain. They pick what is near and leave the rest. I told them our Overseer prefers the far ones. They looked at me with pity, which I resent.

An elf at {retreat} asked me what a strange mood was. I explained: a dwarf is seized by inspiration and demands the one material the fort has just run out of. She said that sounds like a curse. I said it is our proudest tradition.
I am held at {darkfort}, where the goblins keep asking about {past_fort}. They want to know whether it is nice. I said it {past_fort_fate}. They said 'oh good, more room'. I fear for the furniture.

The goblins of {darkfort} have a proper army, with ranks, drills and members who turn up. I have been studying it from my cage. When I get home, I intend to share it all with our captain, if he is awake.

The goblins at {darkfort} have one throne, which their leader sits on, and they are very proud of it. I told them we once had more thrones than dwarves. They called me a liar. I have never felt so homesick.
letters_abroad.by: A Prisoner of Some Standing, at {darkfort}

letters_abroad.body: The goblins at {darkfort} have started reading our obituaries for laughs. They find the thirst ones the funniest. I have asked them to stop. They said if we stopped dying beside barrels, they would have nothing to read.

I have been moved from {darkfort} to {darkfort2}. The food is no better. The cage is no bigger. But there is a window, through which I can see the road home, and on it, as ever, our liaison, recommending an agreement.

The {enemy_race} guards at {darkfort} say {enemy} will march on {fort} soon. They asked how many soldiers we have. I said 'several'. I did not say how many is several. One, technically, is several, if you are hopeful.

Greetings from {hillock}, where my cousins have a still beside every mine shaft. Not one dwarf has died of thirst here in a decade. I asked who designed it. They said 'common sense'. I looked for his office. Nobody by that name works in {fort}.

At {hillock} the work orders are written on a slate and wiped clean when finished. I asked what happens if someone forgets to wipe it. They said 'then you make a few extra'. I told them about {record}. They wiped the slate twice.

The dwarves of {hillock} have a burrow called Safety, too. It is next to the tavern, above ground, and has a door. I asked why it is not thirty levels down. They asked why anyone would put Safety thirty levels down.
{hillock} elected a mayor in an afternoon. There were candidates. There were speeches. There was cake. I have asked for the recipe, for the cake and for the election. They gave me the cake recipe.

Everyone at {hillock} wants news of {fort}. I told them about the mist ring and the windmills. They were impressed. Then they asked about the garbage pit. I said there was no garbage pit. They had already heard about the garbage pit.

I fled {past_fort} when it {past_fort_fate}. {hillock} took me in. I am happy here. I only write because I left a good mug behind, on the second shelf of the dining hall. If anyone goes back, it has my name on it.

I have now visited every corner of {world}. Everywhere I go, someone has heard of us. In one town it was the barrels. In another, the armor stands. In a third, the militia. I have stopped saying where I am from. I say 'a hill'.
Travelling under the banner of {civ}, I was asked at a border how many forts we have founded in this world. I counted on my fingers, then on a friend's. The guard waved me through out of sympathy.

I saw our monarch {monarch} at a feast in {town}. I tried to mention the empty offices at {fort}. A guard said the monarch does not discuss staffing at dinner. I asked when he does. The guard said 'never, at dinner'.

In {town} the walls are rough, the floors are rough and the humans seem perfectly happy. I offered to smooth one wall as a gift. They said it would take too long. I said three smoothers can do sixteen thousand jobs in a lifetime. They left.

{town} has a hangman, who works in a tower, and the tower is used for its purpose. I told them we have a tower but nobody willing. They asked why we built the tower first. I could not say. Nobody can.

The humans of {town} have never experienced a Great Rewind. When I told them that sometimes the world stops and starts again from a moment ago, they called for a doctor. They have one. Of course they do.

I described our mist ring to the elves at {retreat}. They said they have something similar: it is called rain. I said ours is better because it is indoors. They asked why we would bring rain indoors. I am still composing a reply.
{town} has fewer people than {fort} has dwarves, at {pop}, and yet has a mayor, a sheriff, two doctors and a man who just rings a bell. I would settle for the man with the bell.

Word in the cells at {darkfort} is that the goblins who took {past_fort} found our artifacts and use them as doorstops. I asked a guard if this was true. He said only the heavy ones. I have not slept.

The militia captain at {hillock} drills his squad every morning. Eight members. All present. I asked how he does it. He said he simply tells them it is a party. I passed this on to our captain. He is still off duty.
I nearly died of thirst on the road to {town}, beside a cart full of ale I was delivering. It was not my ale. I was not allowed to open it. Now I understand our miners. I owe them all an apology.

I passed through what is left of Padtufted. The Crazed Hex and The Vice of Fins have both been through, and neither tidied up. Refugees asked if {fort} had room. I said yes, and also an armor stand each.
letters_abroad.by: A Traveller, on the Burned Road

letters_abroad.body: Greetings from Toeembrace, where The Fair Cakes do indeed have cakes. I can confirm it. I have eaten four. I have also arranged a modest trade of stone for cake. Please send stone. Please send a bigger wagon.

I passed Searabbeys on the road. The Torments of Hating have put up curtains. Curtains, in our dining hall. Through the window I saw The Nuanced Hamlet on a shelf, beside a goblin's boots. I did not knock.
letters_abroad.by: A Former Searabbeys Hand, Passing By

letters_abroad.body: I have visited Fieryaged to see The Amusing Duties. There is a queue. Every person in it claims the greaves. The keeper gives each claimant a ticket, a number and a long wait. I am number 51. I am optimistic.

The humans of The Grooved Council at Jackaldefense asked if I was with The Distinct Dungeon, the dwarves they evicted. I said no. They seemed relieved. Then they asked if I knew anyone who wanted a slightly used dungeon.
Went back to Quakefocus. The armor stands are still there. All 1,981. Someone has dressed one in a cape. Nobody else lives there except the ghosts, and they seem to be the ones who did the cape.

The dwarves at {hillock} are talking about marching back to {past_fort} and taking it home. They asked whether {fort} would send soldiers. I said we would send our whole army. They asked when he could come. I said after his nap.
The elves of {retreat} are nervous after news of abductions at other retreats. They asked if dwarves could offer protection. I explained our militia. They thanked me and asked the trees instead.

columns.head: THE BARREL DOCTRINE
columns.body: I have lived through more forts than I have teeth. The lesson of all of them fits on a barrel lid: put the drink where the dwarves are. Not near the throne room. Not past the smoothers. Where the dwarves are. I will repeat this until I die, beside a barrel.

columns.head: ON COUNTING ARMOR STANDS
columns.body: Some say a bookkeeper should not interfere with the work orders. I say a bookkeeper who watches the armor stand count pass one thousand without a word is not a bookkeeper. He is a witness. I have filed a note. The note will be ignored. I have counted it.

columns.head: ONE SOLDIER IS A START
columns.body: Critics mock our militia of one. I say every great army begins with one dwarf sitting down. The question is what comes next. In {fort}, what comes next has been 'more sitting'. Still, the foundation is solid. The bench is very solid.

columns.head: IN PRAISE OF EMPTY OFFICES
columns.body: An empty mayor's office files no unfair charges. An empty sheriff's office arrests no innocents. An empty hammerer's office hammers nobody. I begin to suspect our vacancies are the best-run departments in {fort}. Let them stay empty. Let them be our model.

columns.head: THE VIOLATIONS ARE ACCURATE
columns.body: People complain about the production order violations from the mayor's office. Have you checked them? I have. Every one is correct. The item was ordered. The item was not made. That is a violation. Accuracy is not cruelty, even when it arrives weekly.

columns.head: WHAT {past_fort} TAUGHT US
columns.body: {past_fort} lasted {past_fort_years} and then {past_fort_fate}. Young dwarves ask what it taught us. It taught us to keep a barrel by the mine. It taught us to stop orders at ten. It taught us nothing, actually, but the lessons were there to be learned.

columns.head: A FOOTNOTE ON {record}
columns.body: History will judge {record_fort} harshly for {record}. I wish to offer a defence. Every one of those items was well made. Not one was needed, but all were well made. Is that not, in its way, the purest form of dwarven craftsmanship? No? Fine.

columns.head: LET THE LIAISON FINISH HIS SENTENCE
columns.body: Every year {liaison} begins 'There is much to share' and every year someone cuts him off. I propose a trial: one year where we let him finish. What if the second sentence is wonderful? What if it is a recipe? We have never known. We owe it to ourselves.

columns.head: THE ENEMY IS FAR AWAY. GOOD
columns.body: {civ} are at war with {enemy}, and {enemy} are far away. Strategists call this 'luck'. I call it 'distance', which is the cheapest wall ever built. We should not complain about distance. We should thank it, and keep the gate shut.

columns.head: ARE WE READY FOR {enemy}?
columns.body: Readers ask whether {fort} is ready for {enemy}. Let us review. Walls: some. Soldiers: one. Captain's duty status: off. Armor stands: an abundance. If {enemy} attacks by asking where to hang their armor, we will be magnificently prepared.

columns.head: A MONARCH'S SILENCE IS A POLICY
columns.body: We have written to {monarch} about the empty offices many times. No reply has come. Some take this as neglect. I take it as trust. A monarch who does not answer believes we can manage. We cannot, but it is touching to be believed in.

columns.head: THIRST IS A SKILL ISSUE
columns.body: Young dwarves die of thirst beside barrels and everyone blames the Overseer. In my day we blamed ourselves, then the Overseer, then the barrel. I say: teach the young to notice a barrel. A pointing lesson. Five minutes. It would save more lives than a hospital.

columns.head: WORDS MATTER: 'SAFETY'
columns.body: If a burrow is called Safety, dwarves believe it is safe. That belief walks them thirty levels down, past the beast, into the dark. I propose we name burrows honestly. 'Probably Fine'. 'Downstairs'. 'Better Than Here, We Hope'. Honesty saves lives.

columns.head: THE COST OF A SMOOTH WALL
columns.body: I have calculated the cost of one smoothed tile: one moment of one dwarf's life. Sixteen thousand of them is a dwarf's whole life, spent making the fort shinier. I am not against shine. I only note that nobody has ever eaten a wall, however smooth.

columns.head: LET THE REFUGEES IN
columns.body: Bands of refugees wander {world} after the goblin burnings. Some say they will eat our food. I say they will fill our militia, take our offices and haul our refuse. That is three problems solved for the price of a bed each. I call that a bargain.

columns.head: {pop} DWARVES, HOW MANY JOBS?
columns.body: With {pop} citizens, {fort} should be able to fill every office twice over. Instead every office is empty and every dwarf is hauling. The bookkeeper sees the problem clearly: everyone has a job. Nobody has a title. Titles do not haul.

columns.head: KEEP A DRAWER FOR THE GODS
columns.body: Every fort should keep one drawer of oddments: a rough gem, a scrap of plant cloth, a bone, a shell. When the gods send a mood, open the drawer. It costs nothing. It would have saved lives in every fort I have known. Nobody has ever built the drawer.

columns.head: THE TREE QUESTION
columns.body: I have watched dwarves climb trees and not come down. I have watched the elves defend the trees. I have watched the Overseer send miners to the surface regardless. I do not blame the trees. I blame the ladder of choices that ends at a branch.

columns.head: THE GREAT REWINDS ARE GOOD FOR BUSINESS
columns.body: When the world rewinds, we lose a few hours of work. But we also get to redo our mistakes. I have seen a dwarf walk past a barrel, die, the world rewind, and the same dwarf walk past the same barrel. Mistakes, it seems, are not rewound.

columns.head: A PROTOCOL FOR THE PIT
columns.body: I propose a simple drill for the garbage pit. One dwarf throws. One dwarf watches. Nobody climbs in. If anyone is seen climbing in, the watcher shouts. This system needs two dwarves and no training, and it would have kept the catacombs much quieter.

columns.head: THE GHOSTS OF {past_fort} HAVE RIGHTS
columns.body: When {past_fort} {past_fort_fate}, we left the ghosts behind. Nobody asked them. A ghost is still a citizen in spirit. I propose a memorial in {fort}, with a slab for every name, so they have somewhere to visit that is not occupied.

columns.head: GIVE THE OVERSEER A SEASON
columns.body: Every new fort, the dwarves turn on the Overseer within a month. I say give it a season. The early orders are always strange. The middle ones are stranger. The late ones are mostly armor stands. But somewhere in there, sometimes, a mist ring appears.

columns.head: THE HOSPITAL COUNT IS WRONG
columns.body: We count hospitals as a sign of health. We should count doctors. A fort with four hospitals and no doctors has four rooms for dying in, nicely furnished. I have revised the books. Our health score is now 'a chair and some soap'. It was always that.

columns.head: FIFTEEN IN THE SAFETY BURROW
columns.body: Fifteen dwarves died in the Safety burrow at Creaturemirrored, thirty levels down, when a forgotten beast came up the stairs. I knew several of them. They went where the sign told them. Let that be the last sign of its kind in the Chambers of Steel.

columns.head: ON THE CRAZED HEX
columns.body: I have studied The Crazed Hex's campaigns: Padtufted, Pulledrained, Ironcrowds. They do not win through strength. They win because nobody is home. Our fort, I note with concern, is also mostly not home. The captain is off duty.

gossip.text: Corridor talk says {citizen} has been quietly stashing a barrel of ale behind every mine shaft. {citizen} denies it, but has been seen walking the tunnels with a very satisfied expression and suspiciously damp boots.

Insiders report {citizen} and {citizen2} first met while both reaching for the same armor stand, one of several hundred in the stockroom. They now share a bedroom, a mug and, inevitably, an armor stand.

Rumours swirl that {citizen} has a crush on the militia captain and has been loitering near the barracks. The captain, off duty as ever, has not noticed. Friends say this is the most active the barracks has been all year.

Whispers in the tavern say {citizen} is quietly planning to run for mayor. Asked to confirm, {citizen} said 'absolutely not' and then asked how heavy the mayor's paperwork is, which friends consider a yes.

Word is a group of young dwarves dared {citizen} to climb the tall tree by the brook. {citizen} declined, citing history. The group has been told the history. The tree has been told nothing and remains smug.
Sources say {citizen} now takes a route three corridors longer to avoid passing the garbage pit. Asked why, {citizen} said 'reasons'. Everyone knows the reasons. Nobody says them out loud.

It is whispered that {citizen} keeps one rough gem hidden in a sock 'for the next mood'. The jeweler is said to be furious. {citizen} says the jeweler can have it when the gods ask nicely, and not before.

Gossip has it that {citizen} and {citizen2} have been sneaking into the Safety burrow for romantic evenings, it being the one place nobody else goes. Friends call it bold. Others call it a terrible idea.
Several tavern regulars swear that {citizen} blushed when the liaison walked by. {citizen} claims it was the heat of the forge. {citizen} is a fisherdwarf. The forge is on another level.
A cold war has broken out between {citizen} and {citizen2} over who smoothed the finest stretch of corridor. Both claim the same tile. The tile, now polished from both ends, has never looked better.

{citizen} was spotted napping on a spare throne in the storeroom, one of far too many. Witnesses say they looked 'regal, but drooling'. The mayor's office has filed a violation for unauthorised majesty.
Hushed voices in the dormitory claim {citizen} has been chatting nightly with the ghost of a dwarf from {past_fort}. {citizen} says the ghost is good company and very good at cards, though it cheats.

{citizen} has told everyone that their grandmother's mug is still on a shelf in {past_fort}, which {past_fort_fate}. A small fund has been started to retrieve it. So far it holds three coins and a button.
{citizen} has been boasting at the tavern that their family helped make {record} at {record_fort}. Nobody is sure whether this is bragging or a confession. {citizen} also seems unsure.
Tongues are wagging that {citizen} asked {liaison} for an autograph during the last visit. The liaison reportedly signed it 'There is much to share' and recommended an import agreement on the back.
Insiders whisper that {citizen} wrote a love poem to {monarch}. It was returned unopened, with a note recommending an import agreement. {citizen} is said to be heartbroken but has framed the note.
Rumours claim {citizen} is secretly a spy for {enemy}. Evidence offered: {citizen} once frowned at a door. {citizen} says the door deserved it. Most of the fort agrees with {citizen} about the door.

{citizen} and {citizen2} were seen walking slowly through the mist ring together, twice, then a third time. Observers note they came out happy, damp and holding hands. Wedding planners are on standby.

Word is {citizen} has been writing poems to the windmills. The poems are reportedly long and heartfelt. The windmills have not replied, but {citizen} insists the creaking is getting more affectionate.

Gossip circles say {citizen} hosts secret picnics at the top of the execution tower. Guests describe the view as lovely and the atmosphere as 'a bit much'. Invitations are said to be much sought after.
{citizen} and {citizen2} are no longer speaking after a disagreement over what happened just before the last Great Rewind. Each remembers winning. The gods, if they remember, have not said.

Corridor whispers say {citizen} is jealous of {moodname}, who was taken by a strange mood this week. {citizen} has started lingering near workshops looking inspired. So far, nothing. The gods are not fooled.
Insiders say {promoted}, our new {post}, found a stack of old violations in the desk drawer on day one and quietly put it back. Friends say it is the wisest decision made in that office in years.

Word in the workshops is that {masterwright} is unbearable since making that masterwork {masterwork}. They now refer to all other items as 'attempts'. Colleagues are coping by making many more attempts.

One of the new arrivals reportedly asked {citizen} where the Safety burrow was, and was told, in a hushed voice, 'never ask that again'. The migrant has since moved bedrooms twice and slept well both times.
Tongues are wagging after {citizen} spent an entire afternoon at the depot 'inspecting goods'. The goods were a merchant's hat. The merchant has promised to bring a second hat next year.

Nobody has ever seen the militia captain on duty, and now some say the captain is not a dwarf at all but a very convincing armor stand with a beard. {citizen} has offered to check. Nobody has let them.

{citizen} has been visiting the empty hospital every day. Friends feared illness. It turns out {citizen} simply likes the quiet and the soap. A small queue of quiet-lovers has since formed. Still no doctor.
Word is {citizen} has been wearing a homemade sheriff's badge around the fort. Nobody has objected, because nobody else wanted the job. Crime, it is said, has not changed. Neither has the badge.

{citizen} reportedly proposed to {citizen2} by leaving a full barrel at the end of their mining tunnel. It was accepted with tears. Older dwarves say it is the most romantic gesture in the fort's history, by far.

Sources say {citizen} has started a club for dwarves who like the Overseer. Membership is one. Meetings are held in a quiet corner. The club's first motion was to ask for fewer armor stands. It passed.

Rumour has it {citizen} has walked the whole map so many times gathering plants that they now know every bush by name. The bushes, apparently, have started to recognise {citizen} too, and droop politely.
Insiders claim {citizen} has been training the dogs to march in formation, in case the militia never fills up. The dogs reportedly march better than any squad the fort has had, and never go off duty.

Gossip has it that {citizen} spent so long smoothing walls they can now see their reflection in every corridor. They have become insufferably vain. Friends are considering roughing a wall as an intervention.

{citizen} has been caught swimming in the cistern after dark. Asked why, {citizen} said 'someone has to enjoy all that water'. The miners, many of whom are thirsty, have asked to be told where the cistern is.

Word is {citizen} has started giving guided tours of the catacombs. Highlights reportedly include 'the tree miner', 'the pit eight' and 'the burrow fifteen'. Reviews are glowing. Nobody laughs on the way out.

Whispers claim {citizen} keeps a list of every dwarf who died of thirst within sight of a barrel. The list is long. {citizen} says it is not morbid, it is research, and plans to send it to the Overseer.

{citizen} insists a cousin is still living in the ruins of {past_fort}, refusing to leave. Others say that fort {past_fort_fate}. {citizen} says the cousin is very stubborn and has been there {past_fort_years}.
