Tavern talk has it that {enemy} have been seen on the horizon. Several dwarves went to look. It was a herd of goats. {citizen} still claims one goat had a spear. The goat has not been questioned.

{citizen} has begun signing every letter 'a proud citizen of {civ}', including notes to the cook about soup. The cook says the soup has not improved but the correspondence has become much more formal.

Rumour says {citizen} has been sneaking into the manager's office at night to quietly lower the numbers on the work orders. Nobody has complained. In fact, several dwarves have left anonymous thank-you notes.

{citizen} and {citizen2} are said to have bonded over a shared love of uncut gems. They visit the jeweler's together and stand in front of the rough ones, protectively. The jeweler finds it very unsettling.
Word is that the child who once had a strange mood is now insufferable, signing every drawing 'legendary'. {citizen}, the child's babysitter, says the drawings are, unfortunately, quite good.

Hushed voices say {citizen} has started collecting stories of the ghosts of past forts, and plans to write a book. The working title is 'Barrels Nearby'. Publishers are said to be nervous about the ending.
{citizen} challenged anyone in the fort to a duel for the vacant champion's title. Nobody showed up, including {citizen}, who overslept. The title remains vacant. Both parties claim victory.

Rumour says someone found the liaison's diary. Every page reportedly reads 'There is much to share' followed by 'Recommended import agreement'. {citizen} swears there is one page that just says 'sigh'.
Gossip has it that {citizen} has been avoiding the execution tower so firmly that they now walk around it in a wide circle. Others say this is to avoid being asked to be hammerer. It is working.
There is a running bet at the tavern over whether the next burrow will also be named Safety. {citizen} has put a week's wages on 'yes'. {citizen2} on 'Safety Two'. Both expect to win.

{citizen} claims to be able to predict the next strange mood by looking at whatever the fort just ran out of. So far {citizen} has been right twice. The gods have reportedly started to find this annoying.
Tongues are wagging that {citizen} has started carrying two waterskins, a mug and a small barrel at all times. 'History,' {citizen} explains, before rattling away down the corridor like a cart.
Word spreads that {citizen} once charged at a windmill believing it was a giant. {citizen} says the windmill started it. Witnesses agree the windmill did, technically, move first.

{citizen} tells the young ones bedtime stories about famine, day 32, from an older fort. The children love them, and now insist on eating one plant, shared, every evening. Their parents are not amused.
{citizen} insists that since the last Great Rewind, they have had the same conversation with {citizen2} every morning. {citizen2} says this is just what conversation with {citizen} is like.
Breathless reports say the militia captain was seen standing up this week, briefly. Experts say he was reaching for a mug. The fort's hopes, briefly raised, have settled back onto the bench with him.

Gossip has it that the empty mayor's office is haunted, since violations keep appearing with no mayor to write them. {citizen} has offered to sleep there one night to find out. {citizen} has not yet done so.
{citizen} claims to have received a message from the Overseer in a dream. The message was 'smooth'. {citizen} has interpreted it as a call to romance. Others suspect it was a work order.
Word is that {citizen} sleeps beside {artifact} every night 'in case the goblins come for this one too'. The artifact is reportedly well rested. {citizen} is not.

The jeweler is said to have chased {citizen} out of the workshop for whispering 'leave some rough' at every cut. {citizen} has since taken to writing 'LEAVE SOME ROUGH' on the walls, which are smooth, so it shows.
{citizen} has been seen standing guard at the garbage pit, waving off anybody who tries to climb in. Nobody asked {citizen} to do this. The fort has quietly decided that {citizen} is a hero.
One of the refugees who arrived from a burned town has caught the eye of {citizen}. The two share a love of quiet rooms and closed doors. Friends say it is the most sensible romance in the fort.

Rumour says {citizen} has been writing pen-pal letters to a goblin in {enemy}. The goblin writes back. The letters are mostly about weather. Both reportedly enjoy them and neither has mentioned the war.

{citizen} has been handing out homemade medals to any dwarf who drinks when thirsty without being reminded. Medals awarded this week: four. Medals given to miners: none. {citizen} says this is the scandal.

{citizen} and {citizen2}, both smoothers, have announced they will marry once their queues are finished. Their friends have quietly calculated the date. The result has been kept from the couple, out of kindness.
The tavern is buzzing that Iden Loloklolor once ate an entire wheel of cheese while explaining an import agreement and never once paused. {citizen} saw it. {citizen} has not been the same since.

{citizen} swears a great-uncle sat on all 148 thrones of Quakefocus, one per night, out of curiosity. The great-uncle reportedly found the 97th the most comfortable. Nobody has asked why he kept going.
{citizen} claims to be a distant relative of Bomrek Enshalcatten, the miner of Searabbeys. Since then, {citizen} has been offered a drink by every single dwarf in the fort, just in case.
Word is {citizen} has drawn up a map of how to sneak into Searabbeys and steal back The Nuanced Hamlet from The Torments of Hating. The map is very detailed. The route goes through the tavern first.

{citizen} has become an enormous fan of The Oily Boots, the dwarves reclaiming Scaldedarch, and has started oiling their own boots every morning in solidarity. The corridor outside their room is now a hazard.
Rumours swirl that {citizen} has one of the 1,981 armor stands from Quakefocus in their bedroom. {citizen} says it was a gift. {citizen2} says it followed them home. The stand refuses to comment.
{citizen} has quietly added their name to the list of claimants to The Amusing Duties at Fieryaged. Friends ask why. {citizen} says everyone else has, and it seemed rude to be left out.
{citizen} insists they once saw the crooked horror Omo Fewethauyira on a trip near Shadyghosts. Details change with every telling. The horror has grown three heights taller since spring.
{citizen} was told off at the tavern for calling the militia 'the Crazed Hex'. {citizen} says it was a compliment. The captain, who heard, has asked to keep the name. He did not stand up to ask.

{citizen} has started wearing a hat shaped like an armor stand, as a protest against the work orders. Several others have copied it. The Overseer has reportedly noticed and queued two hundred more hats.

Word is {citizen} has framed every production order violation the mayor's office ever sent them. The wall is now full. {citizen} is said to be 'aiming for a second wall' and has begun making crowns badly on purpose.

Tavern regulars claim {citizen} is training in secret to become the second member of the militia. Nobody has seen any training. {citizen} says that is what makes it secret. The captain has offered his bench.

corrections.text: Last issue we said the fort's runaway order produced 'roughly two thousand' armor stands. The bookkeeper insists we print the exact figure. The exact figure is 'too many'. We regret the rounding.
A previous article misstated {record}. The bookkeeper of {record_fort} has written to confirm the figure was, if anything, an undercount. We apologise for understating the scale of the problem.
We previously wrote that {past_fort} 'lasted about a week'. It lasted {past_fort_years}. It only felt like a week. We apologise to its founders, and to its ghosts, who have been in touch.
Our history page claimed {past_fort} was 'abandoned for a nicer view'. In fact it {past_fort_fate}. We regret the error, and the view, which was not that nice either.
Last week we described the Safety burrow as 'the safest place in the fort'. We have since reviewed its history. We now describe it as 'a place'. Readers are asked to update their maps.
Our report that the militia captain was 'on duty' was based on a sighting of him standing up. He was reaching for a mug. He remains off duty. We apologise to anyone who felt briefly protected.
We previously reported the militia as 'ten strong'. It has ten places. One is filled. The other nine are, as one reader put it, 'strong in spirit only'. We regret the arithmetic.
Contrary to last issue's headline, nobody has been elected mayor. The dwarf pictured was sitting in the mayor's chair because it was the only chair free. He has since stood up and gone to lunch.
We previously said the mayor's office files 'a few' production order violations. The bookkeeper has counted. It is several per dwarf. We regret the word 'few', and so does everyone who received one.
Last issue said the nearest barrel to the mines was 'a short walk'. It is 41 tiles, two staircases and a smoothing crew. We apologise to every miner who believed us and set out without a waterskin.
We previously wrote that the miner found in a tree 'was admiring the view'. The miner was stuck. We apologise to the family, and to the tree, which has been unfairly blamed in several letters since.

The sign we printed for the garbage pit read 'IN AND OUT'. It should have read 'IN, NOT OUT'. We regret the error, deeply. A replacement sign has been nailed up, quite high, and well away from the edge.
We reported the smoothing queue at 'several hundred jobs'. It is sixteen thousand. The smoother who supplied the first figure has asked us to note he was 'being hopeful'. We understand.
Last week we said the fort has 'four hospitals and four doctors'. It has four hospitals. The doctors were a typing error for 'chairs'. Patients are advised to bring their own soap and opinions.

We reported last issue that the fort had 'plenty of rough gems'. By the time the paper was printed, the jeweler had cut them all. We apologise to the dwarf in a strange mood who read our report and got her hopes up.
A previous issue said the fort was 'well stocked with plant cloth'. This was based on one scrap and a hopeful thread. We apologise to the child currently in a strange mood, and to her parents.

We previously described seven silk scraps as 'a cloth stockpile'. Seven scraps is a handkerchief, cut up. We regret the description and have been asked to stop using the word 'stockpile' for anything smaller than a bin.
Last issue misquoted the outpost liaison {liaison}. He did not say 'There is little to share'. He said 'There is much to share'. As he always does. We apologise for the misquote and the brief panic.
We stated the liaison asked for rings at 120%. The correct figure was 210%. We transposed the digits. The liaison has written to say he would also accept 312%, if we are offering.
A caption last issue identified a dwarf at the feast as {monarch}. It was a statue of {monarch}. Readers who bowed to it have asked whether the bow still counts. The palace says it does, generously.
We referred to our civilization as 'the dwarves, roughly' in last week's editorial. The correct name is {civ}. The diplomat has asked us to use it, and to stop calling the monarch 'that fellow'.
Last issue referred to {enemy} as 'those rude neighbours'. They are, in fact, our sworn enemy in open war. We regret understating the matter. They are also rude neighbours.

We previously described the soldiers of {enemy} as 'mostly harmless'. They are {enemy_race}, they are at war with us, and they are not harmless at all. Our military correspondent has been sent on a long walk to reflect.
Our report that the war was 'going well' was based on the fact that nobody had attacked us lately. We have since learned that this is because nobody has looked. We regret the optimism.
The number of thrones in the old storeroom was printed as '14'. It is a much larger number. The digit we dropped was the important one. We apologise to the thrones, who have very fragile egos.
Last issue said a dwarf in a strange mood had 'claimed the craftsdwarf's workshop'. The dwarf was a child. The workshop was claimed with a crayon. The resulting artifact is nonetheless magnificent.

Our famine coverage referred to 'famine, day 23'. It was day 32. We transposed the digits, which meant we ended the famine nine days early in print. Readers who ate on day 24 on our advice have our sympathies.
Due to a Great Rewind, last week's issue was printed twice and some readers received it before it was written. We apologise for any spoilers. The ending was 'the cat did it'.

Our report that 'the gods blinked' was meant figuratively. We are now told the gods actually blinked, and the fort stood still for some time. We apologise for the metaphor. It was, it turns out, news.

The mist ring was described last issue as 'a refreshing place to drink'. You cannot drink from the mist ring. You can only stand in it. We apologise to every dwarf who stood in it with their mouth open.
A photograph caption last week identified the windmills as 'giants on the surface'. They are windmills. The dwarf who charged at one on our advice is recovering. The windmill is fine.
Our map labelled the execution tower 'Observation Deck'. That is what one reader calls it. The official name is the execution tower. The view is, however, as described: lovely.
We listed catacomb tours as 'family fun'. They are not family fun. They are a solemn walk past dwarves who died beside barrels, in trees and in pits. We regret the cheerful font.
A previous issue said the cistern was 'ankle deep'. It is considerably deeper. We apologise to the dwarf who stepped in on our advice, and congratulate him on learning to swim so quickly.
We reported that the forgotten beast 'took the long way'. It took the stairs. The stairs were the short way. We apologise for the error and for building stairs so convenient for beasts.
Our weather page said it would be 'a dry day for gathering'. It rained. The Overseer sent everyone out anyway, so the forecast made no difference, but we regret being wrong while it happened.
We said 'a few refugees' had arrived at the gate. It was an entire band from a burned town, with carts. We apologise to them for the word 'few' and to the cook for the lack of warning.
Our feature on the ghosts of {past_fort} listed 'about three'. The real count is larger, and the ghosts have written in to say we left several out. They would like their names spelled properly.
We wrongly credited {record} to this fort. It was {record_fort}. The current fort has its own records, which we will publish as soon as the bookkeeper stops counting armor stands.
We announced last week that a champion had been appointed. A dwarf had in fact won an arm-wrestle at the tavern. The office remains vacant. The arm-wrestle champion asks us to note he is available.
Our report that 'the sheriff made an arrest' referred to a dwarf wearing a homemade badge. The arrest was of a bucket. The bucket has been released. The office remains empty.
We said the hammerer post had been filled. A dwarf had only asked what it involved, and then left very quickly. The post remains open. The tower remains tall. Nobody is volunteering.
Last issue stated the fort had a chief medical dwarf. It has a chief medical chair. We apologise to readers who went to the hospital expecting care and found furniture.

We said the dungeon master's office was 'busy'. It is empty. The noise came from a cat. The cat has been offered the post. The cat has declined, which is still more of an answer than anyone else gave.
We stated the fort had 'tidied up its loose stones'. It moved them to a different corridor. The total number of loose stones is unchanged, and, we are told, slightly higher. We regret the error.

Last issue's front page said drink stocks stood at 'plenty'. The figure is {drinks}. Our reporter was standing next to a barrel at the time and generalised. We regret the error. Please still walk to a barrel.
We previously stated that the drink shortage 'has ended'. It has not. Drink stands at {drinks}. We had confused the still with the smoothing station, which was very busy. We regret the confusion.
Our 'Meat Watch' column reported meat was back on the menu. It was a mushroom cut into a meat shape by a hopeful cook. The Meat Watch resumes. We apologise to the cook, who meant well.
We reported the population as 'roughly a hundred'. The census gives {pop}. Our reporter counted beards in the dining hall and missed everyone who was hauling, which is nearly everyone.
We wrongly reported that {moodname} was 'just in a bad mood'. It is a strange mood. These are very different. One needs a hug. The other needs a rough gem we do not have.

Last issue said {promoted} 'reluctantly accepted' the role of {post}. {promoted} has written to say they accepted it gladly, then read the paperwork, and are now reluctant. We regret getting the order wrong.
We described {masterwright}'s new masterwork {masterwork} as 'pretty good'. {masterwright} has asked us to clarify that it is a masterwork. We clarify. It is extremely good. We regret our restraint.
In last issue's obituary for {deadname}, we gave the wrong cause. We stand corrected and ashamed. We also note, for the record, that there was a barrel within reach. There usually is.

We reported that the caravan had brought 'nothing of interest'. It brought rough gems. By the time our reporter returned, the jeweler had cut them all. The report is now accurate, but for the wrong reasons.
Our welcome page for new migrants omitted the advice 'stay off trees'. We regret the omission and have printed it here, large, in case any of the new arrivals is a miner or is likely to become one.
We attributed the order '16,000 smoothing jobs' to the manager. It came from the Overseer. The manager was only the dwarf who read it out loud, then had to sit down. We apologise to the manager.
We listed 'refuse hauling' under Sport. It is not a sport. Readers who formed teams on our advice are asked to disband immediately and, above all, to stay out of the pit.
We said {artifact} was 'safely locked away'. It is on a table in the dining hall. Someone is using it as a coaster. We apologise to the artifact, and to whoever made it, and to the table.

We gave the year as {year} in the wrong place on the masthead last week, causing several dwarves to believe they had aged a decade overnight. They have not. Most of them look it anyway, after this fort.

Last issue stated the number of armor stands produced at Quakefocus was 1,891. It was 1,981. We transposed the digits and lost ninety armor stands in print. The bookkeeper has found them. All of them.
We wrote that Quakefocus held 184 thrones. It held 148. The extra thirty-six existed only in our typesetter's imagination, where, we are told, they are very comfortable.

Our history page said Searabbeys held 1,949 drinks when Bomrek Enshalcatten died of dehydration. It held 1,994. Either figure was enough. We regret the error, and we regret the barrel nobody walked to.
We misspelled the liaison's name as 'Iden Lolokolor'. It is Iden Loloklolor. He has written, at great length, to confirm this, and to recommend an import agreement for extra letters.
Our account of the Quakefocus carpenter said he died beside '15 rough gems'. It was 150. We dropped a zero. The zero has been found, polished and cut, like everything else in that fort.
We reported that The Crazed Hex 'burned down one town'. It was three: Padtufted, Pulledrained and Ironcrowds. We apologise to the two towns we left out, and to their refugees.

We previously credited the reclaiming of Tametomb to The Oily Boots. It was The Chaste Cudgel. The Oily Boots are reclaiming Scaldedarch. Both groups have asked to be told apart. We have bought a chart.
We printed that the Chambers of Steel are at peace with 61 groups. It is 16. We are, however, still at war with two goblin groups. The diplomat has asked us to proofread numbers more carefully.

Our report on the Creaturemirrored Safety burrow said it was 'three levels down'. It was thirty. We dropped a zero, which made the burrow sound closer and the beast's walk much shorter than it was. We regret the error.

We stated last week that the Overseer had 'cancelled the throne order'. It had paused it. The order has resumed. The storeroom is filling again. We regret the false hope and the brief party held in its honour.

Our report claimed the liaison 'finally finished his speech'. He had stopped to cough. He then resumed from 'There is much to share'. We regret the error and the applause, which he took as encouragement.

obits.text: {deadname}, {prof}, has {cause}. Friends note, with heavy hearts, that a full barrel stood within sight. In their honour, every mourner is asked to drink one mug at the memorial, and then walk to the nearest miner and hand them another.

We mourn {deadname}, a {prof} who personally made more armor stands than anyone could count, because nobody ever told them to stop. They have {cause}. One of their stands will mark the grave. Several hundred others are available as wreaths.

{deadname} has {cause}. A loyal {prof}, they signed up for the militia three times and were told each time that the squad was 'full', despite nine empty places. The captain will attend the funeral, off duty.

{deadname}, {prof}, has {cause}. They received more production order violations than any dwarf in history, each for an item they had never heard of. The mayor's office has sent one last violation, for failing to attend work.

The fort mourns {deadname}, a {prof} who always refused to go to the Safety burrow on principle. They have {cause}, somewhere else entirely. Friends say they would have found this vindicating, if exhausting.

{deadname} has {cause}. A careful {prof}, they never once climbed a tree, never stepped near the garbage pit and never trusted a burrow with a nice name. Fate, it seems, simply came by another corridor.

We remember {deadname}, {prof}, who kept a single rough gem in a sock 'in case the gods asked'. They have {cause}. The gem has been passed on to a friend, with instructions not to let the jeweler near it.

{deadname}, {prof}, has {cause}, with 4,000 smoothing jobs still in their queue. Colleagues have agreed to finish them in tribute. At the current rate, the tribute will be complete in several generations.

{deadname} has {cause}. A tireless {prof}, they walked the whole map in the rain for a single berry more times than anyone can count. Every bush in the region is said to be in mourning, slightly drooping.

{deadname}, {prof}, has {cause}. They were the only dwarf in living memory to let the liaison reach the end of 'There is much to share'. What came next, they never told anyone. The secret goes with them.
The fort mourns {deadname}, a {prof} who sat on every spare throne in the storeroom, one per night, to 'find the good one'. They have {cause} before finishing. The good one remains unidentified.

{deadname} has {cause}. Once seized by a strange mood, this {prof} demanded rough gems in a fort that had cut every last one, and somehow found one in a goblin's pocket. That artifact is still the pride of the fort.

{deadname}, {prof}, has {cause}. In life they visited every one of the fort's hospitals, looking for a doctor. They found soap, several chairs and a traction bench. They left glowing reviews for the soap.

We remember {deadname}, a {prof} who stood guard at the garbage pit for years, shouting at anyone who tried to climb in. They have {cause}. A new volunteer is wanted. The shouting voice need not be as loud, but it helps.

{deadname} has {cause}. A gentle {prof}, they would sit by the windmills every evening and tell them about their day. The windmills creaked louder than usual this week. Some say it is grief. Others say oil.

{deadname}, {prof}, has {cause}. They walked through the mist ring every morning for the happy thought, and every morning tried to drink it. They never once succeeded, and never once stopped trying. A hero of hope.

{deadname} has {cause}. A {prof} who survived {past_fort}, they would tell anyone who listened how it {past_fort_fate}. They lived to see another fort, which they said was 'an improvement, but only just'.
{deadname}, {prof}, has {cause}. In youth they worked at {record_fort}, and helped produce {record}. They never spoke of it without a long sigh. The sigh will be carved on the slab, as requested.

{deadname} has {cause}. A {prof} who always said they would one day face {enemy} in battle, they never did, because the militia never left the barracks. They practised their battle cry in the tavern for years.

We mourn {deadname}, a {prof} who wrote to {monarch} every season about the empty offices. They have {cause}. The final letter is still in the post. Friends hope it arrives. Friends do not expect a reply.

{deadname}, {prof}, has {cause}. A proud citizen of {civ}, they sang the anthem every morning, loudly, in the corridor outside the dormitory. The corridor is quiet now. Several dwarves have admitted they miss it.

{deadname} has {cause}. A kindly {prof}, they were the only dwarf {liaison} called a friend. The liaison has sent a card. It opens 'There is much to share', and then, for once, says nothing else at all.

{deadname}, {prof}, has {cause}. They were the only dwarf who claimed to remember both versions of the week before the last Great Rewind. They said the first version was better. Nobody could prove otherwise.
The fort mourns {deadname}, a {prof} who went up the execution tower every evening to watch the sunset, because nobody else would. They have {cause}. The tower is renamed, unofficially, after them.

{deadname} has {cause}. A devoted {prof}, they swept the catacombs every week and knew every name on every slab, along with how each one died. They will now be swept for, by an apprentice who is already nervous.
{deadname}, {prof}, has {cause}. They swam in the cistern every evening and called it 'the only use of all that water'. Thirsty miners took issue with this, but all agreed they had excellent form.

We remember {deadname}, a {prof} who sat beside the militia captain every evening so he would not be alone in the barracks. They have {cause}. The captain has moved his bench slightly, which is the most he has moved in years.

{deadname} has {cause}. A {prof} who prepared their own coffin years ago and smoothed it lovingly every week. It is the smoothest object in the fort. Mourners are asked not to check their reflection in it at the service.
{deadname}, {prof}, has {cause}. They spent an entire season hauling one stone from one end of the fort to the other and back. The stone will be placed on their grave. It knows the way.

{deadname} has {cause}. A patient {prof}, they helped a child in a strange mood find plant cloth when the fort had none, by unpicking their own sleeve. The resulting artifact bears a small, sleeve-shaped tribute.

The fort mourns {deadname}, a {prof} who brewed through every shortage and kept the barrels full when the Overseer wanted walls smoothed. They have {cause}. Every mug raised this week is, by definition, theirs.

{deadname} has {cause}. A {prof} who came to {fort} with a refugee band after the goblins burned their town, they said the fort felt like home within a week. The fort felt the same about them. Their bed is kept made.

{deadname}, {prof}, has {cause}. With no sheriff appointed, they wore a homemade badge for years and kept order with nothing but a stern look. Crime did not fall, but it did feel watched. The badge will be buried with them.

We remember {deadname}, {prof}, who campaigned tirelessly for a barrel at the end of every tunnel. They have {cause}. Their campaign continues. A barrel has been placed by their grave, and dwarves stop to drink there.

{deadname} has {cause}. A {prof} who claimed to talk nightly with the ghosts of older forts, they are now, presumably, part of the conversation. Friends who sleep near the catacombs report the chatter has grown livelier.

{deadname}, {prof}, has {cause}. They framed every violation the mayor's office ever sent them and filled two walls. Their room will be preserved as a museum of paperwork. Admission is free, but a violation will be filed.

{deadname} has {cause}. One of the founders who arrived with too few plants and no drink, this {prof} survived famine, day 32, and every day after it. They always kept a plant in their pocket. It has been planted for them.
The fort mourns {deadname}, a {prof} who counted every gem the fort ever owned, rough and cut. They have {cause}. The final tally is in their notebook. The last line reads: 'Rough: none. Why.'
{deadname}, {prof}, has {cause}. They trained the dogs to march in formation and always said the dogs were the fort's real army. The dogs have stood at the gate all week. They are, notably, on duty.

{deadname} has {cause}. An optimistic {prof}, they once counted seven silk scraps and declared the fort 'rich in cloth'. They will be wrapped, as they wished, in all seven. It will not cover much, but it is the thought.

We remember {deadname}, a {prof} who was the only dwarf in the fort to defend the Overseer's decisions out loud. They have {cause}. The Overseer has, in a gesture of grief, queued one hundred memorial statues.

{deadname}, {prof}, has {cause}. They claimed the champion's title after winning an arm-wrestle and nobody ever argued. The office stays vacant on paper, but in the tavern, the chair is theirs forever.

{deadname} has {cause}. A thoughtful {prof}, they built a loom room early, before anyone could be seized by a mood without one. Every weaver in {fort} owes them, and every weaver has promised to remember.

{deadname}, {prof}, has {cause}. They warned for years that the stairs down to the deep were far too easy to climb. They were right. The stairs have been made awkward in their memory, and the door strongly worded.

{deadname} has {cause} this {season}. A {prof} who never made more than ten of anything, they believed restraint was a craft. In a fort of runaway orders, theirs was the steadiest hand. Ten mourners, exactly, will attend.

{deadname}, {prof}, has {cause}. They hauled more loose stone than anyone in the fort's history, much of it twice. A slab of their favourite stone will mark the grave. The rest stays loose, as they would have wanted.

We remember {deadname}, a {prof} who slept beside {artifact} every night, in case the goblins came for this one too. They have {cause}. The artifact has been moved closer to the tavern, where others can watch it.

{deadname} has {cause}. A {prof} who threw refuse into the pit for years, they always shouted 'BELL!' before every throw, as there was no bell. The shout lives on. Several haulers owe their lives to it.

{deadname}, {prof}, has {cause}. A diplomat once complimented their beard, and they celebrated the date every year afterwards with a small party. This year's party goes ahead as planned. The beard will be honoured.

The fort mourns {deadname}, a {prof} who cut down more trees than any dwarf in memory and never once climbed one. They have {cause}, firmly on the ground, which they always said was the correct place for a dwarf.

{deadname}, {prof}, has {cause}. A survivor of Quakefocus, they made 211 of the 1,981 armor stands and spent the rest of their life refusing to make a 212th. A plain wooden marker, not a stand, marks the grave.

{deadname} has {cause}. A {prof} who remembered the Meat Watch at Searabbeys, they never once left a meal unfinished. They always said Bomrek Enshalcatten would have wanted them to drink up, and they did.

{deadname}, {prof}, has {cause}. They came to us after The Crazed Hex burned Ironcrowds, carrying only a bucket. The bucket was their proudest possession. It has been filled with ale and set beside the slab.

We mourn {deadname}, a {prof} who could recite Iden Loloklolor's speech word for word, including the cough. They have {cause}. The liaison himself sent a note. It recommended an import agreement, gently.

{deadname} has {cause}. A {prof} who was claimant number 49 to The Amusing Duties at Fieryaged, they never got the greaves. Their claim passes to their heirs, who now have the same chance as the other 48.

{deadname}, {prof}, has {cause}. Old enough to have seen The Nuanced Hamlet before Searabbeys fell to The Torments of Hating, they described it often, and never the same way twice. That, they said, was the nuance.

{deadname} has {cause}. A {prof} who once held Claspedserpent at Quakefocus, they always said the silver mace was 'heavier than it looks and lighter than its reputation'. Their own reputation was the reverse.

{deadname}, {prof}, has {cause}. They once glimpsed Oddom Oltartilesh at a distance and spoke of it for the rest of their life. The monarch has been informed of their passing. A reply is expected eventually, or not.

We remember {deadname}, a {prof} who delivered the Quakefocus Sentinel every morning through famine and armor stands alike. They have {cause}. Their route is now walked by a Herald runner, who is slower.

{deadname}, {prof}, has {cause}. Asked once to make a thousand of something, they made ten, set down their tools and said 'that is plenty'. The Overseer never forgave them. The fort never forgot them. Ten candles will burn.

announcements.text: A healthy baby boy was born this week beside a full barrel. The family insists this was deliberate. 'He will never go thirsty,' said his mother. 'We started him where the drink is.' The miners have sent congratulations and envy.

A baby girl arrived this week in the storeroom, between two armor stands, there being nowhere else in that room to stand. She has been given one as a crib. There are, we are told, several hundred more if she outgrows it.
Twins were born near the mist ring this week. The family reports both babies were calm, damp and smiling. The midwife credits the mist. The father credits the midwife. The mist has not commented.
The fort welcomes a baby boy who, the midwife says, slept through his own birth. Older dwarves have already declared him a natural for the militia. The captain has sent a small bench.
A baby girl was born just before a Great Rewind, and then, the family swears, born again just after it. She is the only dwarf in the fort with two birthdays. She intends to celebrate both, loudly.

A baby boy was born this week to a family that came from {past_fort}. He has been named after a great-grandparent who lived there {past_fort_years}. The family hopes he gets a longer stay in this fort.

A healthy baby girl was born this week, the newest citizen of {civ}. She has a strong grip, a loud cry and, the midwife reports, an unsettling interest in work orders. The bookkeeper has been informed.

A baby boy was born this week, clutching, impossibly, a small rough gem. Nobody knows where it came from. The family has hidden it 'for the next mood'. The jeweler has been kept firmly away from the nursery.

A girl arrived this week in the tavern, as her mother refused to go to the Safety burrow 'on principle'. Mother and child are well. The tavern keeper has offered free milk for life, or until the milk runs out.

A baby boy was born during a windstorm while the windmills creaked overhead. His first sound, the family insists, was a creak. He is being considered for an engineering apprenticeship at the earliest legal age.

Two dwarves who met while warning others away from the garbage pit were married this week. The service was held at a safe distance from the pit. The vows included 'I will never throw while you are below'.

Two smoothers were married this week after finishing, between them, a single corridor. They have promised to finish their remaining queues together. Guests did the maths and wished them a very, very long life.

A wedding was held in the old storeroom this week, among the surplus thrones. Every guest had a throne. The couple had two. The mayor's office filed a violation for 'excessive majesty', framed and hung above the cake.

A couple were married inside the mist ring this week. The ceremony was beautiful, the guests were happy and everyone was soaked. The bride reports her veil 'held up better than expected'. The cake did not.

Two dwarves were married at the top of the execution tower, which the bride insists on calling the Observation Deck. The view was lovely. The guests were nervous. Nobody was executed, which the groom called a good omen.

Two citizens were married this week in a ceremony attended by the liaison, who was passing through. He opened his toast with 'There is much to share' and recommended an import agreement. The couple accepted.
{citizen} and {citizen2} were married this week. Both are said to have proposed at once, beside the same barrel, while thirsty. Guests agreed it was the most practical wedding in the fort's history.
Two dwarves whose families both lived in {past_fort} were married this week. Their grandparents never met there. The couple say they intend to make up for lost time, and to keep a barrel by the bed.

A wedding this week was attended by the full militia: the captain, seated. He was off duty, but the couple said it meant a great deal. The nine empty militia places were given chairs at the back, out of respect.

Two dwarves who met in the catacombs while mourning were married this week. They have asked us to stress that they did not hold the wedding in the catacombs. They held the reception there, which they say is different.

{promoted} has become {post}, filling one of the fort's long-empty offices. The chair was dusted for the first time in years. The outbox contained eleven years of violations. {promoted} has closed the outbox.

Congratulations to {promoted}, now {post}. Friends report {promoted} accepted the post, read the job description, looked at the execution tower and asked to accept it slightly less. The request is under review.
The militia has a second member. A hauler, asked if they wished to enlist, said 'I suppose'. This has been taken as a yes. The captain has shifted along the bench. Strength has doubled overnight.

The bookkeeper has been promoted to 'Senior Bookkeeper' in recognition of years spent counting things nobody needed. Among the bookkeeper's achievements: an exact count of every armor stand. The ceremony was brief.

The fort has appointed its first official Garbage Pit Warden. The duties are to stand near the pit and shout at anyone climbing in. The post comes with a badge, a stool and the fort's quiet gratitude.

A new post, Barrel Officer, has been created to ensure that every mine shaft has a barrel within reach. The first holder has already placed four. Miners have described it as 'the best thing to happen in years'.

The fort has named its first Keeper of the Rough Gem, charged with guarding a single uncut gem against the jeweler until a strange mood demands it. The Keeper sleeps with it under the pillow. The jeweler is furious.

{masterwright} has been named Master Craftsdwarf after completing the masterwork {masterwork}. In their speech, they promised to make 'one of something, very well', and never two thousand of anything. Applause.

With the champion's office still vacant, the fort's cats have appointed one of their own to the post, unofficially. The new champion has defeated three rats and a sock. Nobody has dared to challenge the decision.

The dwarf who has worn a homemade sheriff's badge for years has finally been made sheriff, on the grounds that everyone thought they already were. The badge has been replaced with a real one. It is, if anything, less shiny.

A new wave of migrants arrived this week and were met at the gate with a warm welcome, a mug each and a short talk titled 'Trees, Pits and Burrows: What Not To Do'. Most of them listened. One climbed a tree.

A band of refugees from a goblin-burned town arrived this week with carts and stories. The fort has found them beds, jobs and, in one case, an armor stand. They are said to be settling in, and asking about the mayor.

With the latest arrivals, {fort} now counts {pop} citizens, more than enough to fill every office twice. The empty offices have been notified. They remain empty. The new arrivals have been warned about the chairs.

{liaison}, the outpost liaison, arrived at the depot this week. He opened with 'There is much to share'. Our reporter left before the second sentence. Those who stayed say it was about import agreements.

A caravan arrived this week and offered to buy our surplus thrones. The merchants left with four, having been unable to fit any more in the wagon. The storeroom looks, in the bookkeeper's words, 'unchanged'.

A ghost has arrived in the fort, claiming to be from {past_fort}. It says it walked all the way after that fort {past_fort_fate}. It asks for a bedroom with a view and a barrel. Both have been provided, out of courtesy.

A diplomat of {civ} arrived this week and was given a tour of the fort, including the mist ring, the windmills and the catacombs. The garbage pit was left off the tour. The diplomat asked about it anyway.

A veteran of {record_fort} has moved to {fort}. Asked about {record}, they said only 'I was there' and walked away. They have requested a bedroom with no furniture in it whatsoever, and that request has been honoured.
A deserter from {enemy} has arrived at the gate asking for shelter. Asked why they left, they said the war was 'too organised'. They have been shown our militia, and say they feel at home already.

A litter of puppies has arrived in the kennels. The dogs now outnumber the militia by a wide margin. The kennelmaster says the puppies are already more disciplined than the squad, and much more often on duty.

This week marks the anniversary of the day {past_fort} {past_fort_fate}. A moment of silence will be held in the dining hall. Afterwards, everyone is asked to walk to the nearest barrel and drink, in memory.

Today marks the anniversary of {record} at {record_fort}. The bookkeeper will give a short talk. It is not short. Attendance is voluntary. Several dwarves have asked whether it can be voluntary in the other direction.

The fort marks the anniversary of the day it stopped trusting burrows named Safety. A plaque has been placed at the top of the deep stairs. It reads: 'Burrow (Downstairs)'. It is the most honest sign in the fort.

The militia captain marks ten years in the post this week, all of them off duty. A small ceremony was held in the barracks. The captain attended, seated. He was given a new cushion and a medal for consistency.

The mayor's office celebrates five years without a mayor. The anniversary was marked by the filing of a commemorative production order violation, which was, by all accounts, the office's finest work to date.

The mist ring celebrates one year of pumping water into the air for no reason other than joy. Dwarves are invited to walk through it in celebration. Please do not try to drink it. It still does not work.

The fort marks the anniversary of the first Great Rewind. Several dwarves report having celebrated it twice already. The priests have asked everyone to celebrate only once, to avoid confusing the gods.
Today the founders mark the anniversary of famine, day 32. Each will eat a single plant, shared, in remembrance. Then they will eat a very large dinner, also in remembrance, but of a happier kind.

The fort celebrates another year of the reign of {monarch}, who has never visited, written or been seen. A toast will be raised in the dining hall. A letter about the empty offices will be sent. Tradition.

This week marks another year of war with {enemy}. Neither side has done much. A small ceremony was held at the gate. The captain attended, off duty. {enemy} were not seen, which some consider a victory.

{citizen} and {citizen2} have announced their engagement. The proposal took place at the end of a mining tunnel, where {citizen} had left a full barrel as a surprise. It is said to be the most romantic thing a miner has ever seen.

The militia captain has announced his engagement. The bride-to-be says he proposed without standing up, which she found charming. The wedding will be held in the barracks. Guests are asked to bring their own bench.

Two smoothers have announced their engagement, and say they will marry once their queues are cleared. The bookkeeper has calculated the date. He has refused to tell them, out of kindness, and has bought a gift anyway.
A couple announced their engagement this week after their hundredth walk through the mist ring together. Friends say they will hold the ceremony there, and are already looking into waterproof cakes.

Two dwarves have announced their engagement and promise that the wedding will be held well away from trees, pits and burrows with comforting names. The guest list is long. The venue list is very short.

A couple whose grandparents both fled {past_fort} have announced their engagement. They met at a memorial for that fort and bonded over a shared hatred of loose stones. The wedding will be held in a tidy room.

A refuse hauler and a refuse thrower have announced their engagement. They say they met at the pit, one at the top and one at the bottom, and agreed it was time to stop meeting like that. The fort agrees.
A couple got engaged in the depot while the liaison was speaking, as it was the only way to make him pause. He paused, congratulated them, and then started again from 'There is much to share'.

{moodname}, recently seized by a strange mood, has announced an engagement. Their intended says they proposed in the workshop with the artifact still warm. It is unclear whether the proposal was to them or the artifact.

The dwarf in the homemade sheriff's badge has become engaged. The proposal was made by arrest. The 'charge' was 'stealing my heart'. The fort groaned, then applauded. The bucket that was arrested last year attended.

voxpops.q: How far is your nearest barrel?
answers: Forty tiles. Two staircases. A smoothing crew. Every day.
I carry one. It's a small barrel. It's on my back right now.
I'm a miner. I don't know what a barrel looks like any more.
Right here. I sleep in the drink stockpile. Nobody has noticed.
Near enough to see, too far to reach. The classic.
I'm the brewer. I am the barrel, in a sense.

voxpops.q: What would you do with two thousand armor stands?
answers: Hang one sock on each. That's a lot of socks to find.
Build a wall. A very sad wall.
Sell them to the elves. Ha. No.
Nothing. I'd look at them and think about the choices that led me here.
Arm them. They'd still be a bigger army than ours.
I'm a carpenter. Please don't. I'll have nightmares.

voxpops.q: Would you join the militia?
answers: Is it on duty? No? Then yes, I'd love to.
I'd double the army. That's a lot of pressure.
I went to sign up and the captain was asleep.
I'm a child. They said come back when I'm taller than the bench.
Only if there's a bench. I hear there's a bench.
My dog joined. He's doing very well. He has a rank.

voxpops.q: Would you be mayor?
answers: And read all those violations? No thank you.
I'd be mayor for one day and abolish violations. Then resign.
Yes. Nobody's asked. That's why I'm saying it loudly.
I sat in the chair once. It's very comfortable. I left before it trapped me.
Not until somebody tidies the outbox. It's full of my name.
I'm a cat person. I'd appoint a cat. Is that allowed?

voxpops.q: Where do you go when the alarm rings?
answers: Not the Safety burrow. I'm not stupid.
The tavern. If I'm going, I'm going with a mug.
I keep working. The stone won't haul itself.
Under my bed. It's worked so far.
Up a tree? No. Absolutely not. Never mind.
Wherever the captain is. Then I wake him.

voxpops.q: What would you say to the Overseer?
answers: Please put a barrel near the mines. That's all. Just one.
Thank you for my room. Please finish the other 4,000.
Stop. Just stop. Let us finish one thing.
I'd say 'smooth' and see what happens.
I like the mist ring. Do more of that, less of the thrones.
Nothing. It might give me a work order.

voxpops.q: Have you ever climbed a tree?
answers: Once. I came straight down and never told anyone. Until now.
I'm a miner. I know better. Mostly because of the history pages.
The elves did, they made it look easy. It's not easy.
I'm a woodcutter. I prefer them horizontal.
No. I've seen what's up there. Branches. And regret.
My cousin did. We don't talk about my cousin.

voxpops.q: What's in the garbage pit?
answers: Refuse. And please, leave it there.
I don't know and I'm not going in to find out.
Several ex-haulers' good intentions.
My old boots. I'm not getting them back. I've accepted it.
Things that should stay in a pit. Like the pit.
I'm the Pit Warden. Nothing goes in while you're in it. My rule.

voxpops.q: If you had a strange mood, what would you ask for?
answers: A rock. Something we definitely have. I've read the news.
Rough gems. Just to watch the jeweler cry.
Plant cloth. Then I'd die. So, a rock.
A barrel. Then I'd drink it. Problem solved.
Whatever we just ran out of. That's how it works.
I'm a child. Crayons. I'd ask for crayons.

voxpops.q: Do you remember {past_fort}?
answers: I was born there. It {past_fort_fate}. I don't like to talk about it.
{past_fort_years}. That's how long it lasted. Felt longer.
My gran left her mug there. Second shelf. Still bitter.
Only the stories. They all end with 'and then'.
I remember the loose stones. My feet remember them more.
Yes. The ghosts write to me sometimes. Mostly complaints.

voxpops.q: What do you think of {record}?
answers: I think {record_fort} should have checked the order.
Impressive, in a way. Mostly in a bad way.
My uncle made a lot of them. He has a twitch now.
If I made that many of anything, I'd want a medal. Or a nap.
History will remember it. History should probably move on.
I'd like one. Just one. As a souvenir. Is that wrong?

voxpops.q: What did the liaison say to you?
answers: There is much to share. Then I left.
He recommended an import agreement for my lunch.
He asked about rings at 210 percent. I said I make socks.
Nothing. I hid behind a throne. We have a lot of thrones.
He shook my hand for so long I got a callus.
He said 'There is much'. I interrupted him. I regret nothing.

voxpops.q: Are you afraid of {enemy}?
answers: Not really. They're far away and we're far more disorganised.
The captain says not to worry. From the bench.
A little. I've packed a bag. It's mostly mugs.
No. I'm more afraid of the stairs to the deep.
I've never seen one. I assume they're tall and rude.
I'm a child. I'm afraid of carrots. I'll add them to the list.

voxpops.q: Why will nobody fill the empty offices?
answers: The paperwork. Have you seen the paperwork?
Hammerer comes with a tower. That's not a perk.
I tried to be champion. Nobody came to fight. I went home.
Chief medical dwarf? I faint at blood. I faint at soap.
Because then you have to do the job. Next question.
I'm holding out for 'Keeper of the Mist Ring'.

voxpops.q: Did you notice the last Great Rewind?
answers: I had breakfast twice. Best day of my life.
I lost an afternoon of smoothing. Four tiles. Gone.
No. Did it happen? Has it happened yet?
I won an argument, then the world rewound, then I lost it.
The gods blinked. I blinked back. Fair's fair.
I'm still not sure which version of me this is.

voxpops.q: Have you been through the mist ring?
answers: Every morning. Happy, damp, thirsty. Same as ever.
I tried to drink it. Don't tell anyone.
My beard has never been shinier. I'm a convert.
I prefer my water in a mug, ideally with ale in it.
It's lovely until you remember you're thirsty.
I proposed there. She said yes. Then she sneezed.

voxpops.q: What do you think of the windmills?
answers: Noisy. Lovely. Noisy.
I charged one. I'd rather not discuss the outcome.
They do more work than half the fort.
I like to think they're waving at me.
Giants, obviously. Nobody believes me.
I oil them. They don't thank me. Typical windmills.

voxpops.q: Have you been up the execution tower?
answers: For the view. Only for the view.
I call it the Observation Deck. So does my mother.
No. I don't trust towers with that name.
Yes, for a picnic. Highly recommended. Bring a blanket.
The hammerer job comes with it. That's why it's empty.
I wave from the top. Nobody waves back. Fair enough.

voxpops.q: Do you visit the catacombs?
answers: To pay respects. And to count. It's a lot.
My uncle's there. Died beside a barrel. Classic.
The tour is excellent. The guide is very dramatic.
I go to think. It's the only quiet place in the fort.
No. They're getting crowded. I'll wait my turn.
I'm the sweeper. I know everyone there by name.

voxpops.q: Have you ever been treated at the hospital?
answers: I went to all four. Found chairs, soap and a traction bench.
I treated myself. My arm points mostly the right way now.
There's no doctor. There's a hauler who looks concerned.
Yes. By a cat. It sat on me until I felt better.
The soap is excellent. Best soap in the fort.
No. I just stay healthy, out of spite.

voxpops.q: How long is your smoothing queue?
answers: Longer than my life. I've made my peace.
Sixteen thousand. Ish.
I finished one wall. I cried. It's beautiful.
I'm not a smoother. They gave me one anyway.
I don't count any more. It's healthier.
My grandchildren will finish it. I've told them.

voxpops.q: Where were you sent to gather plants?
answers: The far edge of the map. In the rain.
Everywhere. All of it. Every bush.
Across the river and back for one berry. Someone else ate it.
The surface. In winter. I brought back snow.
Behind my bed. I grow one in secret. Don't tell.
I wasn't. I hid in the tavern. Best season ever.

voxpops.q: Should the jeweler leave some gems rough?
answers: Yes. One. In a drawer. For the gods.
Absolutely. I nearly died of a mood last year.
No. Cut gems are prettier. Moods should ask for those.
I'm the jeweler. I'm only following orders. Sorry.
I've hidden one in my sock. You didn't hear it from me.
The gods should learn to like cut gems. Times change.

voxpops.q: When did you last have a drink?
answers: Just now. I read the obituaries. I'm cautious.
Yesterday? I've been busy. The Overseer gave me a list.
I'm a miner. Define 'last'.
I carry two waterskins and a mug. Every hour.
I'm in the tavern. I'm always having a drink.
I'm the bookkeeper. I'll check the ledger.

voxpops.q: Have you ever sat on a throne?
answers: The spare ones in the storeroom. Very comfy. Regal, even.
I'm a child. I sit on one daily. Nobody stops me.
No. I was told I'd get a violation.
I sat on all of them, one a night. Still looking for the good one.
They're for nobles. We don't have any. So, yes.
I made forty. I've never sat on one. Irony.

voxpops.q: What would you say to the militia captain?
answers: Stand up! Just once! For me!
Thank you for your service. And your bench.
Can I have your job? It looks restful.
Nothing. I didn't want to wake him.
He's a good dwarf. He's just very, very off duty.
I brought him a mug. He accepted it. Our finest hour.

voxpops.q: Should the fort take in more refugees?
answers: Yes. More dwarves, more militia. Maybe.
We've got beds. Plenty of armor stands too.
As long as they bring drink. Just in case.
I was a refugee. Yes. Absolutely yes.
Fine, but not in my corridor. It's full of stones.
Let them in. Maybe one of them will be mayor.

voxpops.q: What do you think of {monarch}?
answers: Never met them. They seem far away.
I wrote to them about the offices. Still waiting.
Very regal, I'm told. I've seen a statue.
I'd like a visit. We have thrones. Many thrones.
Long may they reign. Over there. Quietly.
I'm a child. Is the monarch a cat?

voxpops.q: What makes you proud to be part of {civ}?
answers: Beards. Mostly the beards.
We never give up. On anything. Even when we should.
Our craftsmanship. Two thousand of something, perfectly.
Our ale. Our forts. Our history pages, less so.
The anthem. I sing it every morning. Loudly.
That we keep trying, fort after fort.

voxpops.q: Do you believe in ghosts?
answers: I've met three. One cheats at cards.
My uncle's ghost asked me for a drink. I gave him one.
No. But I sleep with a lamp, in case.
They're just citizens who missed the barrel.
The ones from old forts are the chattiest.
I'm the catacomb sweeper. I believe in all of them.

voxpops.q: Have you seen the cistern?
answers: It's full. Very full. My throat is not.
I fell in. Learned to swim. Got assigned to gather plants.
It's beautiful. Like a lake that never leaves.
It's for emergencies. Like thirst, which is always.
I swim in it at night. Don't tell the miners.
Is that the big wet room? Yes. I've walked past it.

voxpops.q: How has your {season} been?
answers: Busy. I hauled one stone the whole time.
Thirsty. Same as last season.
Lovely. I stayed off trees.
I walked through the mist ring daily. Very damp, very happy.
I gathered one berry in the rain. Someone ate it.
I was off duty. I'm in the militia.

voxpops.q: What advice would you give {promoted}, our new {post}?
answers: Don't open the outbox.
Don't read the work orders. Just don't.
Get a cushion. You'll be sitting a lot.
Hide from the liaison.
Run. While there's still time.
Congratulations! Now you can file violations too.

voxpops.q: What do you think {moodname} will make?
answers: Something wonderful, if we have what they need. We won't.
Something that needs a rough gem. Oh dear.
I hope it's a barrel. A legendary barrel. By the mines.
Something made of the last scrap of plant cloth in the fort.
An armor stand. A very, very good one.
Whatever it is, the goblins will steal it one day.

voxpops.q: Is {fort} home to too many {topanimal}?
answers: We have {topanimal_n}. That's more than our militia, by a lot.
No such thing as too many. Unless they're carp.
They outnumber the soldiers. That says more about the soldiers.
I like them. They're always on duty.
I keep tripping over them. That's not a complaint. Mostly.
Can they be mayor? Asking for a friend.

voxpops.q: Have you seen our {artifact_item}?
answers: Yes. It's lovely. Someone's using it as a coaster.
I sleep next to it. In case goblins come.
Is that the one from the mood? Beautiful work.
I saw it once. Then I needed a sit-down.
We left the last one in an old fort. I'm watching this one.
I touched it. I'm not supposed to say that.

voxpops.q: What should the next fort do differently?
answers: Barrels by the mines. Always barrels by the mines.
No burrow called Safety. Ever.
Stop the orders at ten. Ten is a nice number.
Fill the offices. Any dwarf will do. Any dwarf at all.
Keep one rough gem. In a drawer. Locked.
Stay off trees. Especially miners. Especially the trees.

voxpops.q: Where is the militia captain right now?
answers: The bench. Same as always.
Asleep. Off duty. Peaceful.
He went to the tavern. Big day for him.
He stood up once. I missed it.
In the barracks, beside nine empty places.
Guarding us. Spiritually.

voxpops.q: Would you take the hammerer's job?
answers: No. And I'd like that written down.
Does it come with the tower? Then no.
I'd take it if I never had to do anything. So, maybe.
I asked what it involved. I'm still running.
I'm a gentle soul. I couldn't hammer a nail.
Only if they rename it 'Observation Officer'.

voxpops.q: Have you ever been hungry in a fort?
answers: Famine, day 32. My mother still talks about it.
Once. We shared one plant. It was a small plant.
No. I'm the cook. I eat first. Don't tell.
We had twenty farm plots and no meat. Go figure.
I'm always hungry. That's just being a dwarf.
I ate a mushroom shaped like a steak. It didn't help.

voxpops.q: Do you like the Overseer?
answers: It built the mist ring. So, a bit.
It built two thousand armor stands. So, no.
It's never boring. I'll give it that.
It gave me a bedroom. And forty thousand jobs.
I'm in the fan club. We're a club of one.
No comment. It might be listening.

voxpops.q: Do you remember the armor stands of Quakefocus?
answers: 1,981. I can still hear them creaking.
I made 211 of them. Please don't ask about the other 1,770.
Someone put a cape on one. Best day at Quakefocus.
And the 148 thrones. Don't forget the thrones.
My father counted them every morning. He has a twitch.
I was born under one. Literally under one.

voxpops.q: What do you remember about Searabbeys?
answers: The Meat Watch. Months of it. I still dream of ham.
1,994 drinks and poor Bomrek. Never forget.
The loose stones. 800 of them. All in my corridor.
The goblins have it now. The Torments of Hating. Rude.
The Nuanced Hamlet. It's still there. I miss it.
Thirteen dogs. I don't want to talk about the dogs.

voxpops.q: What do you make of Iden Loloklolor?
answers: There is much to share. That's all I know about him.
He asked me for rings at 210 percent. I'm a fisherdwarf.
He's very consistent. I respect consistency.
Lovely hat. Same speech. Lovely hat.
I've never heard him finish a sentence. I'd pay to.
He recommended an import agreement to my dog.

voxpops.q: What do you think of The Crazed Hex?
answers: Terrible. They burned Padtufted and Ironcrowds.
My cousin fled Pulledrained with a bucket. Still has it.
They're efficient. We're not. That worries me.
Ngumrash Ensebrab sounds like a sneeze.
If they come here, we'll show them our bench.
I'd like them to meet the Vice of Fins and argue.

voxpops.q: Garbage pit, tree branch or Safety burrow: which is worst?
answers: The pit. At least the tree has a view.
The burrow. It lies to you. The pit is honest.
The tree. I'm a miner. It's personal.
All three. Stay in the tavern.
I'd pick the burrow and then not go.
Is there an option four? I'd like option four.
